docs.title: Level 1 · Entry Foundations
docs.text: Goal: learn double-entry accounting, set up a company in TallyPrime, record everyday transactions, and finish with a month of books for a small trading business.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
1. Accounting Fundamentals & the Golden Rules
  2. Getting Started with TallyPrime
  3. Ledgers & Groups
  4. Payment, Receipt, Contra & Journal Vouchers
  5. Sales & Purchase Vouchers
  6. Inventory Basics: Stock Items, Groups & Units
  7. Bank Reconciliation
  8. Core Reports: Day Book, Trial Balance, P&L, Balance Sheet
  9. GST Fundamentals: CGST, SGST, IGST & Registration
  10. Project — One Month of Books for a Trading Business

By the end of this level you'll apply the golden rules of accounting, create a company, ledgers and stock items, record payment, receipt, contra, journal, sales and purchase vouchers, reconcile a bank account, read the Trial Balance, P&L and Balance Sheet, explain how GST works — and you'll have a full month of books for a trading business.

docs.title: 01 · Accounting Fundamentals & the Golden Rules
docs.text: Before touching TallyPrime, you need the logic it automates: double-entry accounting. Every transaction affects at least two accounts — one debited, one credited, for equal amounts. This module teaches the account types, the golden rules and journal entries using our practice business for Level 1: Sri Sai Traders, a stationery wholesaler in Hyderabad.

docs.title: 1. Key terms
docs.text:
1. Capital — money the owner puts into the business.
  2. Assets — what the business owns: cash, bank balance, stock, furniture, amounts customers owe (debtors).
  3. Liabilities — what it owes: loans, amounts owed to suppliers (creditors).
  4. Income — sales, commission received, interest received.
  5. Expenses — purchases, rent, salaries, electricity.
  6. The accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Capital. Every correct entry keeps it balanced.

docs.title: 2. Three types of accounts and the golden rules
docs.text:
1. Personal accounts (people and organisations: Ramesh, HDFC Bank, Capital): Debit the receiver, credit the giver.
  2. Real accounts (things: cash, stock, furniture, buildings): Debit what comes in, credit what goes out.
  3. Nominal accounts (expenses, losses, incomes, gains): Debit all expenses and losses, credit all incomes and gains.

docs.title: 3. Worked journal entries
docs.text:
1. Owner starts business with ₹5,00,000 cash: Cash comes in (real → Dr), Capital is the giver (personal → Cr). Cash A/c Dr 5,00,000 / To Capital A/c 5,00,000
  2. Deposits ₹3,00,000 in bank: Bank receives (personal → Dr), cash goes out (real → Cr). Bank A/c Dr 3,00,000 / To Cash A/c 3,00,000
  3. Buys stationery stock on credit from Lakshmi Paper Mart for ₹80,000: Purchases (nominal expense → Dr), supplier gives (personal → Cr). Purchases A/c Dr 80,000 / To Lakshmi Paper Mart 80,000
  4. Sells goods to Vijay Book Stall on credit for ₹50,000: Vijay receives (Dr), sales income (Cr). Vijay Book Stall Dr 50,000 / To Sales A/c 50,000
  5. Pays rent ₹15,000 by bank: expense (Dr), bank gives (Cr). Rent A/c Dr 15,000 / To Bank A/c 15,000
  6. Receives ₹30,000 from Vijay by UPI: bank receives (Dr), Vijay gives (Cr). Bank A/c Dr 30,000 / To Vijay Book Stall 30,000

docs.title: 4. From journal to final accounts
docs.text:
1. Journal — chronological record of entries.
  2. Ledger — each account's entries grouped together with a running balance.
  3. Trial Balance — list of all ledger balances; total debits must equal total credits.
  4. Profit & Loss Account — incomes minus expenses = profit or loss for the period.
  5. Balance Sheet — assets, liabilities and capital at a date.
  6. TallyPrime does steps 2–5 automatically from your vouchers — but only if each entry is classified correctly.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Account type Debit Credit Personal Receiver Giver Real What comes in What goes out Nominal Expenses & losses Incomes & gains Equation Assets = Liabilities + Capital Check Trial Balance totals match

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Double entry works because every transaction is an exchange: something of value moves from one place to another, so recording both sides keeps the books self-checking. If debits don't equal credits, an error exists. The golden rules are a memory aid for the deeper modern rule — assets and expenses increase with debits; liabilities, capital and income increase with credits — which is exactly how TallyPrime's groups decide where each ledger appears in the reports.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Write journal entries for these Sri Sai Traders transactions and then a Trial Balance: (1) Owner adds ₹1,00,000 more capital by bank transfer; (2) buys a computer for ₹45,000 by cheque; (3) sells goods for cash ₹22,000; (4) pays electricity ₹3,200 in cash; (5) pays Lakshmi Paper Mart ₹50,000 by NEFT. Check that your debit and credit totals match.

docs.title: 02 · Getting Started with TallyPrime
docs.text: TallyPrime is India's most widely used accounting software for small and medium businesses. This module installs it, creates your practice company, and teaches the navigation and shortcuts you'll use every day.

docs.title: 1. Install and choose a mode
docs.text:
1. Download TallyPrime from tallysolutions.com and install it on Windows.
  2. Without a licence, choose Work in Educational Mode — all features work, but voucher dates are limited to the 1st, 2nd and 31st of a month. That's enough for learning; use those dates in exercises.
  3. Licensed users can activate a single-user or multi-user licence; TallyPrime also offers remote and cloud access options.

docs.title: 2. Create the company
docs.text:
1. On the start screen choose Create Company (or press Alt+K → Create).
  2. Fill: Company name "Sri Sai Traders", mailing name, address, State Telangana, Country India, pincode, phone, email.
  3. Financial year beginning from: 1-4-2026; Books beginning from: 1-4-2026.
  4. Base currency: ₹ (INR) is set by default.
  5. Optionally set a TallyVault password (encrypts data — never forget it; it cannot be recovered).
  6. Press Ctrl+A to accept. TallyPrime asks whether to enable GST and other features now — you can do it later via F11.

docs.title: 3. Navigating TallyPrime
docs.text:
1. Gateway of Tally is the home screen with three sections: Masters (Create, Alter, Chart of Accounts), Transactions (Vouchers, Day Book), Utilities and Reports (Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss, Stock Summary, Ratio Analysis, Display More Reports).
  2. Go To (Alt+G) opens a search box from anywhere — type "Ledger", "Sales", "Balance Sheet" and press Enter. It's the fastest way to move.
  3. The top menu bar holds Company (Alt+K), Data (Alt+Y), Exchange (Alt+Z), Go To (Alt+G), Import (Alt+O), Export (Alt+E), Share (Alt+M) and Print (Alt+P).
  4. The right-hand button bar changes with each screen — e.g. F2 date, F11 features, F12 configure.
  5. Esc goes back; Ctrl+A saves/accepts; Alt+C creates a master (like a new ledger) while you're inside a voucher.

docs.title: 4. Features and configuration
docs.text:
1. F11 (Company Features) turns on capabilities: Maintain Inventory, Enable GST, Enable TDS/TCS, Payroll, Cost Centres, Multiple Currencies, Bill-wise entry.
  2. F12 (Configure) changes how a screen behaves — e.g. show more fields in vouchers or more columns in reports.
  3. Keep features minimal at first; enable more as the course introduces them.
  4. Company management — select, shut, alter or create companies — lives under Alt+K (Company); you can keep several companies open and switch between them.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Shortcut Action Alt+K Company menu (create, select, alter) Alt+G Go To (search any screen) Ctrl+A Accept / save Esc Back / cancel Alt+C Create master on the fly F2 / Alt+F2 Change date / period F11 Company features F12 Configure screen Alt+P / Alt+E Print / Export

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: TallyPrime stores each company as a data folder on your computer (path shown under Alt+Y → Data settings). Every voucher you save updates the underlying ledgers and stock records immediately, so reports are always current — there's no separate "posting" step. Features you enable with F11 add fields and reports to the same data, which is why you can switch on GST or payroll later without starting over.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Install TallyPrime in Educational Mode and create "Sri Sai Traders" with Telangana as the state and a financial year starting 1 April. Use Alt+G to open the Chart of Accounts, Balance Sheet and Day Book. Turn on Maintain Inventory via F11 and note three other features available.

docs.title: 03 · Ledgers & Groups
docs.text: In TallyPrime, every account is a ledger, and every ledger belongs to a group. The group decides where the ledger appears — Balance Sheet or Profit & Loss — and how it behaves. Getting groups right is the single most important setup step.

docs.title: 1. Predefined groups
docs.text:
1. TallyPrime ships with 28 groups: 15 primary groups and 13 sub-groups.
  2. Balance Sheet primary groups: Capital Account, Loans (Liability), Current Liabilities, Fixed Assets, Investments, Current Assets, Branch / Divisions, Misc. Expenses (Asset), Suspense A/c.
  3. Profit & Loss primary groups: Sales Accounts, Purchase Accounts, Direct Incomes, Indirect Incomes, Direct Expenses, Indirect Expenses.
  4. Useful sub-groups: Bank Accounts, Bank OD A/c, Cash-in-Hand, Sundry Debtors, Sundry Creditors, Duties & Taxes, Provisions, Reserves & Surplus, Secured Loans, Unsecured Loans, Loans & Advances (Asset), Deposits (Asset), Stock-in-Hand.
  5. Two ledgers exist by default: Cash (under Cash-in-Hand) and Profit & Loss A/c.

docs.title: 2. Create ledgers
docs.text:
1. Alt+G → Create Master → Ledger (or Gateway → Create → Ledger).
  2. Example ledgers for Sri Sai Traders:
Ledger Group Opening balance Capital – Srinivas Capital Account 5,00,000 Cr HDFC Bank Bank Accounts 3,00,000 Dr Vijay Book Stall Sundry Debtors 20,000 Dr Lakshmi Paper Mart Sundry Creditors 0 Rent Indirect Expenses — Freight Inward Direct Expenses — Sales Sales Accounts — Purchases Purchase Accounts —
  1. For debtors/creditors, fill mailing details, state, and later GST registration details and bill-wise settings.
  2. For bank ledgers, add account number, IFSC and branch (used for cheque printing and e-payments later).
  3. Press Ctrl+A to save each.

docs.title: 3. Direct vs indirect
docs.text:
1. Direct expenses/incomes relate to buying or making goods: freight inward, carriage, wages in a factory. They affect gross profit.
  2. Indirect expenses/incomes are running costs and other income: rent, salaries (office), advertising, interest received. They affect net profit.
  3. Misclassifying freight inward as indirect overstates gross profit — a common error.

docs.title: 4. Custom groups and alteration
docs.text:
1. Create your own groups for clearer reports: e.g. "Marketing Expenses" under Indirect Expenses, "Hyderabad Debtors" under Sundry Debtors.
  2. Alter a ledger via Alt+G → Alter Master → Ledger; changing its group moves all its history to the new place in reports.
  3. Chart of Accounts (Alt+G → Chart of Accounts) shows the full group-ledger tree.
  4. Use Multi-ledger creation (Alt+G → Create Master → Multi Ledger) to create many ledgers under one group quickly.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Ledger Correct group Owner's investment Capital Account Bank account Bank Accounts Customer Sundry Debtors Supplier Sundry Creditors GST/TDS payable Duties & Taxes Office rent, salary Indirect Expenses Freight inward, factory wages Direct Expenses Furniture, computer Fixed Assets

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Groups encode accounting classification once, so every voucher posted to a ledger automatically flows to the right report section. The Balance Sheet is simply the closing balances of all Balance Sheet groups at a date; the P&L aggregates the income and expense groups for a period, splitting direct items above gross profit and indirect items below it. That's why a single wrong group silently distorts every report that uses it.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Create all eight ledgers in the table with opening balances, plus: "Electricity" (Indirect Expenses), "Computer" (Fixed Assets), "Unsecured Loan – Friend" (Unsecured Loans) and two more customers and suppliers. Open the Chart of Accounts and the opening Trial Balance (Alt+G → Trial Balance) — check that the Difference in Opening Balances is explained by your entries.

docs.title: 04 · Payment, Receipt, Contra & Journal Vouchers
docs.text: A voucher is how you record a transaction in TallyPrime. This module covers the four core accounting vouchers you'll use for nearly all non-trading transactions.

docs.title: 1. Voucher basics
docs.text:
1. Open vouchers with Alt+G → Vouchers (or Gateway → Vouchers), then pick the type with function keys: F4 Contra, F5 Payment, F6 Receipt, F7 Journal, F8 Sales, F9 Purchase.
  2. Change the date with F2 (in Educational Mode use 1st, 2nd or 31st).
  3. TallyPrime offers single-entry mode (Account at top, particulars below) or double-entry mode (Dr/Cr lines). Toggle via F12 → Use single entry mode for Payment/Receipt/Contra.
  4. Always write a narration explaining the transaction — auditors and your future self will thank you.

docs.title: 2. Payment voucher (F5) — money going out
docs.text:
1. Paid rent ₹15,000 from HDFC Bank: Account = HDFC Bank; Particulars = Rent ₹15,000.
  2. Paid Lakshmi Paper Mart ₹50,000 by NEFT: Account = HDFC Bank; Particulars = Lakshmi Paper Mart ₹50,000.
  3. Paid electricity ₹3,200 in cash: Account = Cash; Particulars = Electricity ₹3,200.
  4. TallyPrime warns if cash would go negative — a useful control.

docs.title: 3. Receipt voucher (F6) — money coming in
docs.text:
1. Received ₹30,000 from Vijay Book Stall by UPI: Account = HDFC Bank; Particulars = Vijay Book Stall ₹30,000.
  2. Received commission ₹4,000 in cash: Account = Cash; Particulars = Commission Received (Indirect Incomes) ₹4,000.
  3. Bank receipts can capture transaction type (UPI, NEFT, cheque) and instrument details — useful for bank reconciliation.

docs.title: 4. Contra (F4) and Journal (F7)
docs.text:
1. Contra records transfers between cash and bank accounts only:
  2. Deposited cash ₹40,000 into HDFC Bank: Account = HDFC Bank; Particulars = Cash ₹40,000.
  3. Withdrew ₹10,000 cash from bank for office use: Account = Cash; Particulars = HDFC Bank ₹10,000.
  4. Journal records adjustments that don't involve cash or bank:
  5. Depreciation on computer ₹4,500: Dr Depreciation (Indirect Expenses) / Cr Computer.
  6. Goods worth ₹2,000 taken by owner for personal use: Dr Drawings (Capital Account) / Cr Purchases.
  7. Outstanding salary ₹25,000 at month end: Dr Salary / Cr Salary Payable (Current Liabilities).
  8. Rule of thumb: cash/bank involved → Payment, Receipt or Contra; not involved → Journal (credit sales/purchases use Sales/Purchase vouchers, next module).

docs.title: 5. Edit, delete and duplicate
docs.text:
1. Find vouchers in the Day Book (Alt+G → Day Book). Select and press Enter to alter.
  2. Alt+D deletes; Alt+X cancels (keeps the voucher number with zero value for audit continuity); Alt+2 duplicates a voucher.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Voucher Key Use Contra F4 Cash ↔ bank, bank ↔ bank Payment F5 Money out (cash/bank) Receipt F6 Money in (cash/bank) Journal F7 Non-cash adjustments Delete / Cancel / Duplicate Alt+D / Alt+X / Alt+2

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Voucher types are templates that enforce the right accounts: Payment and Receipt require a cash or bank ledger on one side, Contra allows only cash and bank ledgers, and Journal excludes them by default. Each saved voucher posts debit and credit amounts to the ledgers instantly and updates every report. Voucher numbering per type, with cancellations preserved, creates the continuous audit trail that statutory auditors and GST officers expect.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Record these vouchers for Sri Sai Traders (use allowed dates): rent ₹15,000 by bank; electricity ₹3,200 cash; receipt ₹30,000 from Vijay by UPI; commission received ₹4,000 cash; deposit ₹40,000 cash into bank; depreciation ₹4,500 on the computer; outstanding salary ₹25,000. Then open the Day Book and the Cash and HDFC Bank ledgers to check balances.

docs.title: 05 · Sales & Purchase Vouchers
docs.text: Buying and selling goods are the heart of a trading business. This module records purchases and sales in TallyPrime — first in accounting invoice mode (amounts only), then item invoice mode with inventory (after Module 6, you'll use items routinely).

docs.title: 1. Purchase voucher (F9)
docs.text:
1. Bought goods on credit from Lakshmi Paper Mart, Bill No. LPM/221, ₹80,000.
  2. Open F9 Purchase. Set Supplier invoice no. and date (important for GST and payments later).
  3. Party A/c name: Lakshmi Paper Mart; Purchase ledger: Purchases.
  4. In accounting invoice mode, enter the amount ₹80,000. Add freight ₹1,500 as an additional ledger line (Freight Inward, Direct Expenses) if it's on the same bill.
  5. Narration: "Purchase of notebooks and pens, bill LPM/221". Save with Ctrl+A.
  6. For cash purchases, select Cash as the party ledger.

docs.title: 2. Sales voucher (F8)
docs.text:
1. Sold goods on credit to Vijay Book Stall, ₹50,000.
  2. Open F8 Sales. TallyPrime numbers sales invoices automatically.
  3. Party A/c name: Vijay Book Stall; Sales ledger: Sales.
  4. Enter the amount; add any extra charges (e.g. packing charges collected, under Indirect Incomes) as separate lines.
  5. Print the invoice with Alt+P (configure logo, bank details and terms under print configuration).
  6. For cash sales, choose Cash as the party.

docs.title: 3. Item invoice mode (with inventory)
docs.text:
1. With Maintain Inventory on, press Ctrl+H (Change Mode) in the voucher and choose Item Invoice.
  2. Select the stock item, enter quantity and rate; TallyPrime calculates the amount and updates stock.
  3. Example sale: 200 Classmate notebooks @ ₹45 = ₹9,000; 100 Reynolds pens (boxes of 10) @ ₹60 = ₹6,000; total ₹15,000.
  4. Add discounts per line (enable via F12) or as a separate Discount Allowed ledger.

docs.title: 4. Orders, delivery and receipt notes (overview)
docs.text:
1. Larger businesses track the cycle: Purchase Order → Receipt Note (goods received) → Purchase invoice, and Sales Order → Delivery Note → Sales invoice.
  2. Enable via F11 → Enable Order Processing. Delivery Note (Alt+F8) and Receipt Note (Alt+F9) record goods movement before billing.
  3. Outstanding orders reports show what's pending — useful for wholesalers like Sri Sai Traders.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Task Path / key Purchase F9 Sales F8 Accounting vs item invoice Ctrl+H (Change Mode) Supplier invoice no. Enter on every purchase Print invoice Alt+P Delivery / Receipt Note Alt+F8 / Alt+F9 Order processing F11

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: A sales voucher posts a debit to the customer (or cash) and a credit to the sales ledger; with inventory, it also reduces stock quantity and records the outward movement at the item's cost for valuation. Purchase vouchers do the reverse. Because the party, invoice number, date and items are captured in one record, TallyPrime can later produce GST returns, outstanding reports and stock statements from the same data — which is why accurate invoice details matter far beyond the entry itself.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Record: purchase from Lakshmi Paper Mart ₹80,000 + freight ₹1,500 (bill LPM/221); cash purchase ₹6,000; credit sale to Vijay Book Stall ₹50,000; cash sale ₹22,000; credit sale to another customer ₹18,500. Print one sales invoice. Check the Sales and Purchase registers (Alt+G → Sales Register / Purchase Register).

docs.title: 06 · Inventory Basics: Stock Items, Groups & Units
docs.text: For a trading business, stock is usually the largest asset. TallyPrime's inventory module tracks quantities, values and movement of every item. This module sets up units, stock groups and items, and records stock-based vouchers.

docs.title: 1. Units of measure
docs.text:
1. Alt+G → Create Master → Unit.
  2. Simple units: Nos (numbers), Box, Kg, Pcs, Ream. Set the symbol and decimal places (0 for Nos).
  3. Compound units: Box of 10 Nos — lets you sell in boxes and track pieces.
  4. For GST later, map each unit to the official UQC (Unit Quantity Code), e.g. Nos → NOS-NUMBERS.

docs.title: 2. Stock groups and categories
docs.text:
1. Stock groups organise items: Notebooks, Pens, Paper, Art Supplies.
  2. Stock categories (optional, F11/F12) add a second classification such as brand: Classmate, Reynolds, JK Paper.
  3. Create via Alt+G → Create Master → Stock Group / Stock Category.

docs.title: 3. Stock items
docs.text:
1. Alt+G → Create Master → Stock Item.
  2. Fill name ("Classmate Notebook 172 pages"), group (Notebooks), category, unit (Nos).
  3. Opening balance: quantity 500, rate ₹38 → value ₹19,000.
  4. Later you'll add GST details (HSN code and rate) on items.
  5. Set standard rates (cost/selling price) if your business uses fixed price lists.

Example items for Sri Sai Traders:

Item Group Unit Opening qty Rate Classmate Notebook 172 pages Notebooks Nos 500 38 Reynolds Pen Box (10) Pens Box 200 52 JK Copier A4 Ream Paper Ream 150 230

docs.title: 4. Recording stock movement
docs.text:
1. Purchases (F9) and sales (F8) in item invoice mode update quantities automatically.
  2. Stock Journal (Alt+F7) transfers or converts stock — e.g. damaged items moved to a "Damaged" item, or repacking.
  3. Physical Stock voucher (Ctrl+F7) records actual counted quantities; TallyPrime adjusts book stock to match.
  4. Enable godowns/locations later (Level 3) if stock is kept in more than one place.

docs.title: 5. Inventory reports
docs.text:
1. Stock Summary (Alt+G → Stock Summary): quantity, rate and value of every item.
  2. Stock Item vouchers: movement history for one item.
  3. Movement Analysis: which items sell fastest.
  4. Reorder status (after setting reorder levels): items to buy.
  5. Valuation method defaults to Average Cost; others (FIFO, Last Purchase Cost) are set per item (Level 3).

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Master / voucher Path or key Unit Create Master → Unit Stock Group / Category Create Master → Stock Group / Category Stock Item Create Master → Stock Item Stock Journal Alt+F7 Physical Stock Ctrl+F7 Stock Summary Alt+G → Stock Summary

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: When inventory is integrated with accounts, every item-based voucher updates both quantity and value. Closing stock is calculated automatically using the item's valuation method and flows into the Balance Sheet (as an asset) and the P&L (reducing cost of goods sold). That integration means stock errors become profit errors — an unrecorded sale overstates stock and understates profit, which is why periodic physical counts and the Physical Stock voucher matter.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Create the three units, four stock groups and the three items above with opening stock. Record an item-wise purchase of 300 Classmate notebooks @ ₹39, an item-wise sale of 250 notebooks @ ₹48 and 50 pen boxes @ ₹65, and a physical stock count showing 498 reams of A4 instead of the book quantity. Review the Stock Summary.

docs.title: 07 · Bank Reconciliation
docs.text: Your books and the bank statement rarely match on any given day — cheques take time to clear, banks deduct charges you haven't recorded, customers pay directly into your account. Bank reconciliation explains every difference and catches errors or fraud early.

docs.title: 1. Why differences occur
docs.text:
1. Cheques issued but not yet presented — recorded in books, not yet in the bank.
  2. Cheques deposited but not yet cleared — in books, not yet credited by the bank.
  3. Bank charges, interest, GST on charges — in the statement, not yet in books.
  4. Direct deposits / UPI collections you haven't recorded.
  5. Errors — wrong amount or wrong ledger in books.

docs.title: 2. Reconcile in TallyPrime
docs.text:
1. Open the bank ledger: Alt+G → Bank Reconciliation, choose HDFC Bank (or open the bank ledger and use the Reconcile option).
  2. The screen lists vouchers with a Bank Date column. For each entry that appears in your bank statement, enter the date the bank processed it.
  3. Entries without a bank date remain unreconciled.
  4. At the bottom TallyPrime shows Balance as per Company Books, Amounts not reflected in bank, and Balance as per Bank. Compare the last with your statement's closing balance.
  5. If they don't match, look for statement entries missing from your books.

docs.title: 3. Record missing entries
docs.text:
1. Bank charges ₹590 (₹500 + 18% GST): Payment voucher — Account HDFC Bank; Particulars Bank Charges ₹500 and Input GST (if you claim it) ₹90.
  2. Interest credited ₹1,200: Receipt voucher — HDFC Bank / Interest Received (Indirect Incomes).
  3. Direct UPI from a customer ₹8,000: Receipt voucher — HDFC Bank / customer ledger.
  4. Return to reconciliation and set bank dates for these entries.

docs.title: 4. Auto reconciliation and statements
docs.text:
1. TallyPrime supports importing bank statements (Excel or supported formats, and connected banking for supported banks) to match entries automatically.
  2. Review suggested matches carefully, then accept.
  3. Unmatched statement lines become a to-do list of vouchers to create.
  4. Reconcile at least monthly, ideally weekly for active accounts.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text: Item Amount (₹) Balance as per books 2,15,400 Dr Less: cheques deposited not cleared (18,000) Add: cheques issued not presented 12,500 Less: bank charges not recorded (590) Add: interest not recorded 1,200 Balance as per bank statement 2,10,510

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Situation Action Entry in both books & statement Set bank date In books, not in statement Leave unreconciled (timing) In statement, not in books Create voucher, then reconcile Error in books Alter voucher Auto match Import statement, review matches

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Reconciliation compares two independent records of the same account. Timing differences resolve themselves as cheques clear; missing entries and errors don't, and reconciliation is the control that exposes them. In TallyPrime, the bank date doesn't change your accounting date — it only marks when the bank processed the entry, so the books keep the true transaction date while the reconciliation report proves the bank balance.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Using your HDFC Bank ledger, assume a bank statement that shows all your entries except one ₹18,000 cheque deposit and one ₹12,500 cheque issued, plus bank charges ₹590 and interest ₹1,200 not in your books. Record the missing vouchers, set bank dates, and confirm that the "Balance as per Bank" matches the statement.

docs.title: 08 · Core Reports: Day Book, Trial Balance, P&L, Balance Sheet
docs.text: TallyPrime's value is in its reports — always up to date, with drill-down from totals to individual vouchers. This module teaches you to read the essential reports and use them to check your work.

docs.title: 1. Day Book
docs.text:
1. Alt+G → Day Book lists all vouchers for a date or period (Alt+F2 to change period).
  2. Use it daily to review entries; press Enter on any voucher to open and correct it.
  3. Filter by voucher type with F4 or configure columns with F12.

docs.title: 2. Ledger and group summaries
docs.text:
1. Ledger report (Alt+G → Ledger) shows all entries for one account with running balance — e.g. Vijay Book Stall's account statement.
  2. Group Summary (e.g. Sundry Debtors) lists all customers with balances — who owes how much.
  3. Cash/Bank Books show cash and bank movement.

docs.title: 3. Trial Balance
docs.text:
1. Alt+G → Trial Balance shows closing balances of all groups; press Alt+F1 (Detailed) or expand groups to see ledgers.
  2. Total debits must equal total credits. A "Difference in opening balances" line means opening balances don't agree — fix them in ledger masters.
  3. Scan for oddities: a supplier with a debit balance (overpaid?), cash with a credit balance (impossible), expenses in the wrong group.

docs.title: 4. Profit & Loss Account
docs.text:
1. Alt+G → Profit & Loss A/c for the period.
  2. Top section (trading account): Opening stock + Purchases + Direct Expenses vs Sales + Closing stock → Gross Profit.
  3. Lower section: Gross Profit + Indirect Incomes − Indirect Expenses → Net Profit.
  4. Example (illustrative one-month figures): Sales ₹1,35,000; Opening stock ₹99,400; Purchases ₹86,000; Freight inward ₹1,500; Closing stock ₹1,08,200 → Cost of goods sold ₹78,700 → Gross profit ₹56,300. Rent ₹15,000, salary ₹25,000, electricity ₹3,200, depreciation ₹4,500, commission received ₹4,000 → Net profit ₹12,600.

docs.title: 5. Balance Sheet
docs.text:
1. Alt+G → Balance Sheet at a date: Capital and liabilities on one side, assets on the other.
  2. Net profit appears under Profit & Loss A/c on the liabilities/capital side.
  3. Drill down from Current Assets → Sundry Debtors → a customer → vouchers.
  4. Use F12 to show percentages, comparative periods (Alt+C to add a column) or vertical format.

docs.title: 6. Export and share
docs.text:
1. Alt+E exports to Excel, PDF, JSON or XML; Alt+M emails or shares; Alt+P prints.
  2. Save report views with your preferred configuration for repeated use.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Report Answers Day Book What was entered today/this period? Ledger Full history of one account Group Summary Balances of all customers/suppliers Trial Balance Do debits equal credits? Any odd balances? Profit & Loss Gross and net profit for a period Balance Sheet Financial position on a date

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: All TallyPrime reports are views computed from the same voucher data, filtered by date and grouped by the group hierarchy — nothing is stored separately, so a corrected voucher instantly corrects every report. The P&L summarises income and expense groups over a period, while the Balance Sheet captures balances at a point in time; profit is the bridge between them, flowing from the P&L into capital. Drill-down is how accountants audit: start from a surprising total and follow it to the vouchers behind it.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Open the Trial Balance, P&L and Balance Sheet for Sri Sai Traders after all your Level 1 entries. Check that debits equal credits, identify gross and net profit, and drill down to find the voucher behind one expense. Export the Balance Sheet to Excel and PDF.

docs.title: 09 · GST Fundamentals: CGST, SGST, IGST & Registration
docs.text: Goods and Services Tax (GST) is India's indirect tax on the supply of goods and services, levied at each stage with credit for tax already paid. Before configuring it in TallyPrime (Level 2), you need the concepts. Rates and thresholds below are as of 2026 — always confirm the latest notifications on gst.gov.in and cbic-gst.gov.in.

docs.title: 1. How GST works
docs.text:
1. GST is a value-added tax: each business collects tax on its sales (output tax) and deducts tax paid on its purchases (input tax credit, ITC), paying the government the difference.
  2. Example: Sri Sai Traders buys notebooks for ₹10,000 + 5% GST = ₹500 tax. It sells them for ₹14,000 + 5% = ₹700 tax. It pays ₹700 − ₹500 = ₹200 to the government — tax on the ₹4,000 value it added.
  3. The final consumer bears the full tax; businesses act as collectors.

docs.title: 2. CGST, SGST/UTGST and IGST
docs.text:
1. Intra-state supply (seller and place of supply in the same state): tax split equally into CGST (Central) + SGST (State) — or UTGST in Union Territories. 18% = 9% CGST + 9% SGST.
  2. Inter-state supply (different states) and imports: IGST at the full rate (18% IGST).
  3. Place of supply rules decide which applies — for goods, generally where delivery ends; for many services, the recipient's location.
  4. Sri Sai Traders (Telangana) selling to Hyderabad → CGST + SGST; selling to Bengaluru, Karnataka → IGST.

docs.title: 3. Rates and codes
docs.text:
1. Following the September 2025 rate rationalisation, most goods and services fall into 5% (merit/essential items) or 18% (standard), with 40% for specified luxury and sin goods, plus nil/exempt items and special rates (e.g. 3% on gold). Check each item's current rate.
  2. Goods are classified by HSN codes; services by SAC codes. Invoices must show HSN/SAC (4 digits for turnover up to ₹5 crore, 6 digits above, as currently required).
  3. Using the wrong HSN or rate leads to short payment, interest and penalties.

docs.title: 4. Registration
docs.text:
1. Registration is mandatory when aggregate turnover exceeds ₹40 lakh for goods suppliers (₹20 lakh in special category states) and ₹20 lakh for service providers (₹10 lakh in special category states).
  2. Some must register regardless of turnover: inter-state suppliers of goods, e-commerce sellers (with limited exceptions), casual taxable persons, those liable under reverse charge, and others.
  3. Register on gst.gov.in with PAN, Aadhaar authentication, business proof and bank details; you receive a 15-character GSTIN (state code + PAN + entity number + check digit), e.g. 36ABCDE1234F1Z5 (36 = Telangana).
  4. Small businesses may opt for the Composition Scheme (Level 2, Module 7).

docs.title: 5. Key returns (overview)
docs.text:
1. GSTR-1 — details of outward supplies (sales), monthly by the 11th (or quarterly under QRMP).
  2. GSTR-2B — auto-generated statement of ITC available from suppliers' filings.
  3. GSTR-3B — summary return with tax payment, monthly by the 20th (staggered dates for quarterly filers).
  4. GSTR-9 — annual return.
  5. Interest applies on late payment and late fees on late filing.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Term Meaning Output tax GST on sales ITC Credit for GST paid on purchases CGST + SGST Intra-state supply IGST Inter-state supply, imports HSN / SAC Codes for goods / services GSTIN 15-character registration number GSTR-1 / 3B Sales details / summary + payment

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: GST taxes consumption at each stage but only on the value added, because every registered buyer offsets tax paid upstream through input tax credit. The split between CGST/SGST and IGST routes revenue to the right governments: IGST collected on inter-state sales is settled to the consuming state, preserving GST's destination-based design. The credit chain depends on matching — your ITC is backed by your supplier's reported sales (visible in GSTR-2B) — which is why accurate invoicing and timely supplier filing affect your own tax liability.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: For Sri Sai Traders (Telangana), calculate GST and the tax split for: (1) sale of notebooks ₹20,000 at 5% to a Hyderabad shop; (2) sale of printer paper ₹50,000 at 18% to a Chennai buyer; (3) purchase of office chairs ₹30,000 at 18% from a Hyderabad supplier. Compute net GST payable for the month assuming full ITC eligibility. Decode GSTIN 36ABCDE1234F1Z5.

docs.title: 10 · Project — One Month of Books for a Trading Business
docs.text: Put Level 1 together: record a full month of transactions for a new trading business in TallyPrime and produce its reports. (GST is configured in Level 2, so this month uses amounts excluding tax.)

docs.title: 1. Company setup
docs.text:
1. Create Kaveri Kitchenware (Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu), financial year from 1 April 2026, with inventory enabled.
  2. Create ledgers: Capital – Anitha (₹6,00,000 Cr), Canara Bank, Cash, Rent, Salary, Electricity, Freight Inward, Discount Allowed, Interest Received, Furniture, Sales, Purchases, Salary Payable; customers: Home Needs Store, Annapoorna Hotel; suppliers: Prestige Distributors, Steelcraft Industries.
  3. Create units (Nos, Set), stock groups (Cookware, Utensils) and items: Pressure Cooker 5L (opening 40 @ ₹1,450), Non-stick Tawa (60 @ ₹520), Steel Plate Set (30 sets @ ₹780).

docs.title: 2. Transactions for the month
docs.text:
1. Capital ₹6,00,000: ₹4,50,000 deposited in Canara Bank, ₹1,50,000 cash (opening + Contra).
  2. Bought furniture ₹38,000 by bank transfer.
  3. Purchased 50 pressure cookers @ ₹1,420 from Prestige Distributors on credit; freight inward ₹1,200 cash.
  4. Purchased 40 tawas @ ₹500 from Steelcraft Industries on credit.
  5. Sold 30 pressure cookers @ ₹1,950 and 25 tawas @ ₹720 to Home Needs Store on credit.
  6. Sold 12 steel plate sets @ ₹1,100 to Annapoorna Hotel for cash.
  7. Received ₹40,000 from Home Needs Store by NEFT, allowing ₹500 discount.
  8. Paid Prestige Distributors ₹60,000 by cheque.
  9. Paid rent ₹18,000 and electricity ₹2,900 by bank.
  10. Salary for the month ₹30,000: ₹20,000 paid in cash, ₹10,000 outstanding.
  11. Interest credited by bank ₹350; bank charges ₹236.
  12. Physical count: 2 tawas damaged — record via Stock Journal to a "Damaged Stock" item or as a loss.

docs.title: 3. Reconcile and review
docs.text:
1. Reconcile Canara Bank assuming the ₹60,000 cheque hasn't been presented yet.
  2. Review the Day Book; fix any errors.
  3. Check the Trial Balance balances and has no odd balances.

docs.title: 4. Reports to produce
docs.text:
1. Stock Summary with closing quantities and values.
  2. Profit & Loss Account — note gross profit and net profit.
  3. Balance Sheet at month end.
  4. Outstanding balances of customers and suppliers (Group Summary).
  5. Export all reports to PDF/Excel.

docs.title: Deliverable checklist
docs.text: Item Done? Company, ledgers, items with opening balances All 12 transaction groups recorded with narrations Bank reconciliation completed Trial Balance agrees Stock Summary, P&L, Balance Sheet exported One-paragraph summary of results

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: This project mirrors a real month-end: transactions flow in from bank, cash, sales and purchases; reconciliation and stock counts verify them against independent evidence; and the reports summarise performance and position. The order matters — reconciling and checking the Trial Balance before reading profit ensures the numbers you report are trustworthy. Employers testing Tally skills usually give exactly this kind of task.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Complete the month for Kaveri Kitchenware, then write a short management summary: sales, gross profit margin (%), net profit, cash and bank position, top-selling item, and amounts receivable and payable. Keep this company — you'll add GST to similar transactions in Level 2.

docs.title: Level 2 · Intermediate GST in Practice
docs.text: Goal: run GST end to end in TallyPrime — compliant invoices, input tax credit, monthly returns, notes, e-invoices and e-way bills — and track receivables and costs.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
1. GST Setup in TallyPrime
  2. GST Invoicing: HSN/SAC, Tax Rates & Place of Supply
  3. Input Tax Credit & GSTR-2B Reconciliation
  4. GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B Returns
  5. Credit Notes, Debit Notes & Sales Returns
  6. E-Invoicing & E-Way Bills
  7. Reverse Charge & the Composition Scheme
  8. Bill-wise Details: Receivables & Payables
  9. Cost Centres & Budgets
  10. Project — A GST-Compliant Month for a Wholesaler

By the end of this level you'll configure GST in TallyPrime, raise compliant invoices with HSN/SAC and place of supply, reconcile ITC with GSTR-2B, prepare GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B, issue credit and debit notes, generate e-invoices and e-way bills, handle reverse charge and composition, manage bill-wise receivables, use cost centres — and complete a GST-compliant month for a wholesaler.

docs.title: 01 · GST Setup in TallyPrime
docs.text: With GST concepts in place, this module configures TallyPrime to calculate, record and report GST automatically. Our Level 2 practice company is Godavari Wholesale Mart, a registered regular taxpayer in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, trading in household goods.

docs.title: 1. Enable GST for the company
docs.text:
1. Press F11 (Company Features) and set Enable Goods and Services Tax (GST) to Yes.
  2. In the GST details (or Alt+K → GST → Show More in recent releases): State Andhra Pradesh, Registration type Regular, GSTIN (e.g. 37ABCDE1234F1Z9 — 37 is Andhra Pradesh), Applicable from 1-4-2026.
  3. Set Periodicity of GSTR-1: Monthly (or Quarterly if you've opted for QRMP).
  4. Enable options as relevant: e-Way Bill applicable (and threshold), e-Invoicing applicable (if your aggregate turnover requires it — Module 6), and Tax Liability on Advance Receipts.
  5. Save with Ctrl+A.

docs.title: 2. Tax ledgers
docs.text:
1. Create under group Duties & Taxes, Type of duty/tax: GST, with the matching Tax type:
Ledger Tax type Output CGST Central Tax Output SGST State Tax Output IGST Integrated Tax Input CGST Central Tax Input SGST State Tax Input IGST Integrated Tax
  1. Some businesses use single CGST/SGST/IGST ledgers for both input and output; separate ledgers make reconciliation clearer.
  2. Leave the percentage blank on tax ledgers so TallyPrime picks the rate from item or ledger GST details.

docs.title: 3. Sales and purchase ledgers
docs.text:
1. Alter Sales and Purchases ledgers: GST applicability: Applicable, set Nature of transaction if needed (e.g. "Sales Taxable" — TallyPrime decides intra/inter-state from the party's state).
  2. Create separate ledgers if you have distinct types: Sales – Exempt, Sales – Exports, Purchases – Imports.
  3. GST rates are best set on stock items (next section), with ledgers left to inherit them.

docs.title: 4. Party and item GST details
docs.text:
1. For each customer/supplier ledger: Registration type (Regular, Composition, Unregistered/Consumer, SEZ, Overseas), GSTIN/UIN, State, and address. TallyPrime validates GSTIN format.
  2. For each stock item (or stock group): HSN/SAC code and description, Taxability (Taxable, Exempt, Nil-rated), GST rate (e.g. 18% → CGST 9% / SGST 9% / IGST 18% shown automatically), and Type of supply (Goods/Services).
  3. Use stock group level GST details when many items share the same HSN and rate — items inherit them.
  4. For services, create service ledgers (e.g. "Repair Services Income") with SAC and rate.
  5. TallyPrime's GST Rate Setup screen lets you review and update rates for many items at once.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Setting Where Enable GST, GSTIN, state, periodicity F11 / Alt+K → GST Tax ledgers Duties & Taxes, Type = GST, Tax type Sales/Purchase ledger GST applicable Party details Registration type, GSTIN, state Item details HSN/SAC, taxability, rate Bulk rate review GST Rate Setup

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: TallyPrime decides GST on each invoice by combining three facts: your company's state, the party's state (or place of supply), and the item's taxability and rate. Same state → CGST and SGST at half the rate each; different state → IGST at the full rate. Because rates live in masters (items, groups or ledgers) with effective dates, a rate change can be applied from a specific date without touching old invoices — critical after events like the 2025 rate rationalisation.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Create Godavari Wholesale Mart with GST enabled (monthly GSTR-1). Create the six tax ledgers, GST-applicable Sales and Purchases ledgers, three customers (one in Andhra Pradesh, one in Telangana, one unregistered consumer) and two suppliers with GSTINs, and five stock items with HSN codes and current rates (look up actual rates for items such as steel utensils, LED bulbs, plastic buckets, detergent and pressure cookers on the CBIC rate finder).

docs.title: 02 · GST Invoicing: HSN/SAC, Tax Rates & Place of Supply
docs.text: A GST invoice must contain specific details, and TallyPrime calculates tax automatically once masters are right. This module records intra-state, inter-state, B2B and B2C sales and purchases correctly.

docs.title: 1. Mandatory tax invoice contents
docs.text:
1. Supplier name, address and GSTIN.
  2. Consecutive serial number unique for the financial year (up to 16 characters) and date.
  3. Recipient name, address and GSTIN (for registered buyers); for unregistered buyers above certain values, name, address and state.
  4. HSN/SAC, description, quantity, unit, value, discount, taxable value.
  5. Tax rate and amount separately for CGST, SGST/UTGST, IGST.
  6. Place of supply (state name) for inter-state supplies.
  7. Whether tax is payable on reverse charge, and signature.
  8. For unregistered buyers or composition dealers, a Bill of Supply is used when no tax is charged (e.g. by composition dealers or for exempt goods).

docs.title: 2. Intra-state sale (CGST + SGST)
docs.text:
1. F8 Sales → Party: Srinivasa Stores, Vijayawada (registered, Andhra Pradesh).
  2. Item: Steel Kadai 20 pcs @ ₹600 = ₹12,000 (18%).
  3. Add Output CGST and Output SGST ledgers below items — TallyPrime fills ₹1,080 each.
  4. Invoice total ₹14,160. Print with Alt+P; the invoice shows HSN, rates and tax split.

docs.title: 3. Inter-state sale (IGST)
docs.text:
1. Party: Sai Ram Traders, Hyderabad (Telangana, registered).
  2. Item: LED Bulbs 9W 500 pcs @ ₹70 = ₹35,000 at the item's GST rate.
  3. Add Output IGST — at 18%, ₹6,300; total ₹41,300.
  4. TallyPrime sets Place of Supply: Telangana from the party; you can change it in party details if goods are delivered elsewhere (e.g. "bill to" one state, "ship to" another — enter dispatch and consignee details).

docs.title: 4. B2C sales and purchases
docs.text:
1. Walk-in customer (unregistered): use a Cash or "Retail Customer" ledger with registration type Unregistered/Consumer; tax is calculated the same way.
  2. Inter-state B2C invoices above ₹1 lakh are reported individually in GSTR-1 (B2CL); smaller B2C sales are summarised (B2CS).
  3. F9 Purchase from a registered supplier: enter supplier invoice number and date exactly as on their bill, items, and Input CGST/SGST or Input IGST. These must match the supplier's GSTR-1 for your ITC.

docs.title: 5. Check invoice-level GST
docs.text:
1. Use Alt+G → GSTR-1 later to see how each invoice is classified (B2B, B2CL, B2CS, exports).
  2. Open any voucher and press Ctrl+O (Related Reports) or view Tax Analysis (via Ctrl+I/More Details in recent releases) to see the tax break-up.
  3. If a voucher shows as "uncertain" or "incomplete" in GST reports, it lacks details (GSTIN, HSN, state) — fix the masters or voucher.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Scenario Tax Notes Same state, registered buyer CGST + SGST B2B in GSTR-1 Different state, registered IGST Place of supply = buyer state Unregistered, inter-state > ₹1 lakh IGST B2CL Unregistered, other As applicable B2CS summary Purchase Input CGST/SGST or IGST Match supplier invoice no.

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Each GST invoice becomes a data record that flows to your GSTR-1 and, from there, to your buyer's GSTR-2B as eligible ITC. That chain is why invoice numbers, dates, GSTINs and HSN codes must be exact — a typo on your sale can deny your customer their credit. TallyPrime classifies invoices into GSTR-1 tables automatically based on registration type, place of supply and invoice value, and flags records with missing information before you file.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: In Godavari Wholesale Mart, record: an intra-state B2B sale, an inter-state B2B sale to Telangana, an inter-state B2C sale above ₹1 lakh, a cash B2C sale, and two purchases (one intra-state, one inter-state). Print one invoice of each type and verify the tax split. Open GSTR-1 and confirm each sale's table.

docs.title: 03 · Input Tax Credit & GSTR-2B Reconciliation
docs.text: Input tax credit (ITC) lets you reduce GST payable by the GST you paid on business purchases. It's valuable — and closely policed. This module covers eligibility, blocked credits, and reconciling your books with GSTR-2B every month.

docs.title: 1. Conditions for claiming ITC
docs.text:
1. You hold a valid tax invoice or debit note.
  2. You've received the goods or services.
  3. The supplier has reported the invoice in their GSTR-1 and it appears in your GSTR-2B.
  4. The supplier has paid the tax to the government.
  5. You've filed your GSTR-3B.
  6. Claim within the time limit: by 30 November following the end of the financial year (or the annual return date, if earlier).
  7. Pay the supplier within 180 days of the invoice date; otherwise reverse the ITC (with interest) and re-claim when paid.

docs.title: 2. Blocked credits (Section 17(5) — examples)
docs.text:
1. Motor vehicles for personal transport (with exceptions such as dealers, driving schools, passenger transport businesses).
  2. Food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, club memberships — unless used for making the same outward supply or provided under a legal obligation.
  3. Works contracts and goods/services for constructing immovable property (other than plant and machinery) on your own account.
  4. Goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off or given as free samples or gifts.
  5. Goods or services for personal consumption.
  6. In TallyPrime, record ineligible ITC on purchase ledgers/items marked Ineligible so it isn't claimed.

docs.title: 3. Understanding GSTR-2B
docs.text:
1. GSTR-2B is a static monthly statement on the GST portal (generated around the 14th) showing ITC available from suppliers' GSTR-1/IFF filings, imports and more.
  2. It shows ITC available and not available (e.g. late or ineligible) and supplier details.
  3. The Invoice Management System (IMS) on the portal lets recipients accept, reject or keep pending inward invoices before GSTR-2B is finalised — review it monthly.

docs.title: 4. Reconcile in TallyPrime
docs.text:
1. Download GSTR-2B (JSON) from the portal, or use TallyPrime's connected GST features to fetch it directly.
  2. In TallyPrime: Alt+G → GSTR-2B Reconciliation (or GSTR-2A/2B under the GST reports menu) → Import the file.
  3. TallyPrime matches portal records with your purchase vouchers by GSTIN, invoice number, date and amounts, showing: Matched, Partially matched (e.g. amount or date differs), Available only in books, Available only in portal.
  4. Investigate each mismatch:
  5. Only in books → supplier hasn't filed; follow up before claiming.
  6. Only in portal → you missed recording the purchase (or it's not yours — reject in IMS).
  7. Partial → typo in invoice number/date or different amounts; correct your voucher or ask the supplier to amend.
  8. Claim ITC in GSTR-3B only for eligible, matched invoices.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Check Rule Documents Valid invoice, goods/services received Supplier compliance In GSTR-2B, tax paid Time limit 30 Nov of next FY (or annual return date) Payment Within 180 days or reverse Blocked Sec 17(5) items Monthly Review IMS, reconcile 2B with books

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: The GST system links every buyer's credit to a seller's declared sale. GSTR-2B is the portal's authoritative view of what the government will accept as your ITC for the period, built from your suppliers' filings — and GSTR-3B's ITC claims are compared against it. Regular reconciliation turns that system into a control: it catches supplier non-compliance early (while you can still press them to file) and prevents excess claims that would attract interest and penalties.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Create a sample GSTR-2B reconciliation for Godavari Wholesale Mart with eight purchase invoices: five that match, one only in books, one only in the portal, and one with a different invoice number. Write the action for each, calculate eligible ITC for the month, and identify which of these purchases would be blocked: a staff lunch, a delivery van for goods transport, a laptop, and gifts to dealers.

docs.title: 04 · GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B Returns
docs.text: Every regular GST taxpayer files two core returns: GSTR-1 (details of sales) and GSTR-3B (summary and payment). This module prepares both from TallyPrime and walks through filing on the portal. Confirm current due dates and forms on gst.gov.in.

docs.title: 1. Due dates and periodicity
docs.text:
1. GSTR-1: monthly by the 11th of the next month; or quarterly under QRMP (turnover up to ₹5 crore) by the 13th after the quarter, with optional IFF for B2B invoices in the first two months so buyers get credit sooner.
  2. GSTR-3B: monthly by the 20th; QRMP taxpayers file quarterly (22nd or 24th depending on state) and pay monthly via PMT-06.
  3. Late fees and 18% interest on late tax apply — file on time even with nil activity (nil returns can be filed by SMS).

docs.title: 2. Prepare GSTR-1 in TallyPrime
docs.text:
1. Alt+G → GSTR-1 for the month.
  2. Review Return View: B2B invoices, B2CL, B2CS, exports, credit/debit notes (registered and unregistered), nil/exempt supplies, advances, HSN summary and documents issued.
  3. Resolve uncertain transactions (missing GSTIN, HSN, place of supply, rate) before export.
  4. Export the return as JSON (Alt+E) and upload to the portal's offline tool, or upload directly with TallyPrime's connected GST features.
  5. On the portal: Returns → GSTR-1 → Prepare online/upload, check summary, file with DSC or EVC (OTP).

docs.title: 3. Prepare GSTR-3B
docs.text:
1. Alt+G → GSTR-3B for the same month.
  2. Key tables:
  3. 3.1 Outward taxable supplies (taxable value and tax), zero-rated, nil/exempt, inward supplies under reverse charge.
  4. 3.2 Inter-state supplies to unregistered persons, composition dealers (by state).
  5. 4 Eligible ITC — from imports, RCM, and all other ITC — minus reversals; matched to GSTR-2B.
  6. 5 Exempt/nil/non-GST inward supplies.
  7. 6 Payment of tax.
  8. On the portal, values are auto-populated from your GSTR-1 and GSTR-2B; compare them with TallyPrime's computation and resolve differences. Recent portal changes restrict editing auto-populated liability — correct errors through GSTR-1A/next GSTR-1 amendments as the portal guides.

docs.title: 4. Pay the tax
docs.text:
1. Worked example for the month: Output CGST ₹48,000, SGST ₹48,000, IGST ₹62,000. Eligible ITC: CGST ₹31,000, SGST ₹31,000, IGST ₹70,000.
  2. Set-off order: IGST credit first against IGST liability, then CGST and SGST (in any order or proportion); CGST credit against CGST then IGST; SGST credit against SGST then IGST. CGST and SGST credits can't be used against each other.
  3. IGST credit ₹70,000: ₹62,000 against IGST, remaining ₹8,000 against CGST → CGST liability left ₹40,000 − ₹31,000 CGST credit = ₹9,000 cash; SGST ₹48,000 − ₹31,000 = ₹17,000 cash.
  4. Deposit cash via PMT-06 challan (UPI, net banking, NEFT/RTGS) into the electronic cash ledger, then offset in GSTR-3B and file.
  5. In TallyPrime, record the set-off with a Journal (output vs input tax ledgers) and the payment with a Payment voucher (Stat Payment details: GST, period).

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Return Content Due (monthly) GSTR-1 Invoice-level sales 11th GSTR-3B Summary + tax payment 20th IFF B2B invoices (QRMP months 1–2) 13th PMT-06 Monthly payment (QRMP) 25th Set-off IGST → CGST/SGST; CGST ↛ SGST

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: GSTR-1 is the source data the system uses to build every buyer's GSTR-2B and to auto-populate your own GSTR-3B liability, so accuracy in GSTR-1 drives everything else. GSTR-3B is where tax is actually paid: liabilities are offset first using credits in a legally prescribed order (IGST credit is used first because it's shared between the Centre and states), with the balance paid in cash. TallyPrime's role is to make the books, the returns and the payment entries agree.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: For Godavari Wholesale Mart, generate GSTR-1 for your Level 2 transactions, fix any uncertain items and export JSON. Prepare GSTR-3B, compute the set-off for the month using your figures, and record the set-off journal and the cash payment voucher.

docs.title: 05 · Credit Notes, Debit Notes & Sales Returns
docs.text: Invoices sometimes need correction after issue: goods returned, price reduced, discount given after sale, or additional charges. Under GST you never edit an issued invoice to change its tax value — you issue a credit note or debit note. This module records them correctly.

docs.title: 1. When to use which
docs.text:
1. Credit note (issued by the supplier) reduces the taxable value or tax of an earlier invoice: sales return, post-sale discount agreed in advance and linked to invoices, price reduction, invoice overcharged.
  2. Debit note (issued by the supplier) increases value: undercharged price, additional charges.
  3. A buyer may issue a "debit note" to a supplier for purchase returns in commercial practice, but under GST the tax adjustment is driven by the supplier's credit note.
  4. Time limit for GST credit notes: by 30 November following the end of the financial year (or the annual return date, if earlier).

docs.title: 2. Sales return / credit note in TallyPrime
docs.text:
1. Enable F11 → Use Debit/Credit Notes (and inventory tracking if items are returned).
  2. Press Ctrl+F8 (Credit Note).
  3. Party: Srinivasa Stores; select original invoice number and date (Reference details — required for GST reporting).
  4. Item: Steel Kadai 5 pcs @ ₹600 = ₹3,000; Output CGST ₹270 and SGST ₹270 reversed. Total ₹3,540.
  5. Narration: "Return of 5 damaged kadais against Inv. GWM/045".
  6. Stock increases by 5 (or post to a damaged-stock item via a stock journal).

docs.title: 3. Price reduction without return
docs.text:
1. Use the credit note in accounting invoice mode with the sales ledger and tax ledgers, or item mode with zero quantity and value only (configure via F12).
  2. Example: agreed 5% discount on Inv. GWM/051 (₹40,000 + IGST ₹7,200): credit note ₹2,000 + IGST ₹360.
  3. Discounts not linked to specific invoices or not agreed before supply don't reduce GST value — record them as commercial credit notes without GST.

docs.title: 4. Debit note and purchase returns
docs.text:
1. Ctrl+F9 (Debit Note) for: (a) your own debit note to a customer for additional charges with GST; or (b) recording a purchase return to a supplier — reference the supplier's original invoice and reverse input tax.
  2. Purchase return example: returned 10 LED bulbs @ ₹70 = ₹700 to an inter-state supplier → Input IGST ₹126 reversed. Your ITC drops when the supplier's credit note appears in GSTR-2B.

docs.title: 5. Reporting
docs.text:
1. Credit/debit notes to registered parties appear in GSTR-1 CDNR; to unregistered parties above thresholds in CDNUR; and they adjust GSTR-3B tables.
  2. Supplier credit notes reduce your ITC in GSTR-2B.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Situation Voucher Key Sales return Credit Note Ctrl+F8 Post-sale discount (pre-agreed, linked) Credit Note Ctrl+F8 Undercharged / extra charges Debit Note Ctrl+F9 Purchase return (record) Debit Note Ctrl+F9 Always reference Original invoice no. & date Time limit 30 Nov of next FY

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: GST is reported invoice by invoice, so corrections must also be traceable documents linked to the original supply. A credit note reduces the supplier's output tax and, through GSTR-1 and GSTR-2B, simultaneously reduces the buyer's eligible ITC — keeping both sides of the credit chain consistent. Editing an already-reported invoice would break that link, which is why returns and price changes are always recorded as separate notes.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Record for Godavari Wholesale Mart: a sales return of 5 kadais, a pre-agreed 5% discount credit note on an inter-state invoice, a debit note for ₹1,000 extra freight charged to a customer with GST, and a purchase return to a supplier. Check how each appears in GSTR-1 and in the party ledgers.

docs.title: 06 · E-Invoicing & E-Way Bills
docs.text: Two electronic systems sit alongside GST invoices: e-invoicing, which registers B2B invoices with a government portal, and e-way bills, which document goods in transit. TallyPrime can generate both directly. Thresholds are as of 2026 — confirm on einvoice.gst.gov.in and ewaybillgst.gov.in.

docs.title: 1. E-invoicing basics
docs.text:
1. Mandatory for taxpayers whose aggregate annual turnover exceeds ₹5 crore in any financial year since 2017-18 (certain sectors like banks, insurers, SEZ units and GTAs are exempt).
  2. Applies to B2B invoices, exports, and credit/debit notes to registered persons — not B2C invoices (those may need a dynamic QR code above a higher turnover threshold).
  3. The invoice is reported to the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP), which validates it and returns an IRN (Invoice Reference Number), an acknowledgement number and date, and a signed QR code that must be printed on the invoice.
  4. Taxpayers with turnover of ₹10 crore and above must report invoices to the IRP within 30 days of the invoice date.
  5. E-invoice data flows automatically into the supplier's GSTR-1 and can auto-generate an e-way bill.

docs.title: 2. E-invoicing in TallyPrime
docs.text:
1. In company GST details, set e-Invoicing applicable: Yes and the applicable date.
  2. Ensure masters are complete: party GSTIN, address, pincode, state; item HSN; unit mapped to UQC.
  3. On saving a sales invoice, TallyPrime offers to Send for e-Invoicing (connected services require a Tally.NET/IRP login setup with your GSP credentials).
  4. TallyPrime stores the IRN, acknowledgement and QR code and prints them on the invoice.
  5. Cancel an IRN within 24 hours if needed (cancel on IRP, then in TallyPrime); after that, issue a credit note.
  6. The e-Invoice report lists invoices pending, sent, rejected or cancelled.

docs.title: 3. E-way bill basics
docs.text:
1. Required for movement of goods where the consignment value exceeds ₹50,000 (some states have different limits for intra-state movement), with exemptions for certain goods.
  2. Part A: GSTINs of supplier and recipient, place of delivery, invoice number/date, value, HSN, reason for transport.
  3. Part B: transporter details — vehicle number (road) or transport document number (rail, air, ship).
  4. Validity depends on distance: generally 1 day per 200 km for regular cargo (20 km per day for over-dimensional cargo).
  5. The person causing movement (usually the supplier, or the transporter/recipient) generates it.

docs.title: 4. E-way bills in TallyPrime
docs.text:
1. Enable e-Way Bill in GST details with the threshold limit and applicable date.
  2. In the sales invoice, fill e-Way Bill details: transporter, distance (pincode-based), mode, vehicle number.
  3. Generate online through TallyPrime's connected services or export JSON for upload on the e-way bill portal.
  4. Update Part B if the vehicle changes; extend validity before expiry if transit is delayed.
  5. The e-Way Bill report shows bills pending generation, generated and expiring.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Item Rule (2026) E-invoice threshold AATO > ₹5 crore Output IRN + signed QR on invoice 30-day reporting AATO ≥ ₹10 crore IRN cancellation Within 24 hours E-way bill threshold Consignment > ₹50,000 (state variations) E-way validity ~1 day per 200 km

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: E-invoicing moves invoice reporting to the moment of issue: the IRP validates the invoice's structure and the supplier's identity, stamps it with a unique IRN and passes the data to the GST and e-way bill systems. This reduces fake invoices and data mismatches because buyers' credit is based on validated records. E-way bills track goods physically moving, letting tax officers verify consignments on the road against declared invoices; the e-invoice-to-e-way-bill link means one accurate entry serves both.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: For Godavari Wholesale Mart (assume turnover above ₹5 crore), configure e-invoicing and e-way bills, complete all required master fields, and prepare one B2B invoice with e-invoice and e-way bill details (vehicle, distance 275 km). State the e-way bill validity and the latest time the IRN could be cancelled.

docs.title: 07 · Reverse Charge & the Composition Scheme
docs.text: Normally the supplier charges and pays GST. Under the reverse charge mechanism (RCM), the recipient pays instead. Small businesses may also choose the simplified Composition Scheme. This module handles both in TallyPrime. Rules and lists are as of 2026 — verify current notifications.

docs.title: 1. Reverse charge — when it applies
docs.text:
1. Notified services (examples): goods transport agency (GTA) services to specified recipients (when GTA hasn't opted to pay tax itself), legal services by advocates to businesses, services by directors to the company, sponsorship services to body corporates, security services by non-corporate suppliers to registered persons, and renting of commercial property by an unregistered person to a registered person.
  2. Notified goods (examples): cashew nuts (not shelled), tendu leaves, certain tobacco leaves, silk yarn, raw cotton, when supplied by specified suppliers.
  3. Imports of services are generally under RCM (IGST paid by the importer).
  4. Specified procurements from unregistered suppliers by certain sectors (e.g. real estate promoters) also attract RCM.

docs.title: 2. Accounting for RCM
docs.text:
1. The recipient issues a self-invoice (for supplies from unregistered persons) and a payment voucher to the supplier.
  2. Tax under RCM must be paid in cash (electronic cash ledger) — ITC can't be used to pay it.
  3. The recipient can then claim the same amount as ITC if eligible, so the net cost is usually cash flow timing.
  4. Report in GSTR-3B Table 3.1(d) (liability) and Table 4 (ITC).

docs.title: 3. RCM in TallyPrime
docs.text:
1. Create the expense/service ledger (e.g. "Legal Fees") with GST details: SAC, rate and Applicable for reverse charge: Yes.
  2. Record the purchase voucher from the supplier; TallyPrime calculates the RCM tax and marks the liability.
  3. Use TallyPrime's Stat Adjustment journal ("Increase of Tax Liability & Input Tax Credit" for reverse charge) — or the automated RCM handling in recent releases — to book tax liability and ITC.
  4. Example: advocate fees ₹50,000 (intra-state, 18%) → RCM liability CGST ₹4,500 + SGST ₹4,500; pay ₹9,000 in cash with GSTR-3B; claim ₹9,000 ITC.

docs.title: 4. Composition Scheme
docs.text:
1. Eligibility: aggregate turnover up to ₹1.5 crore (₹75 lakh in special category states) for goods suppliers and restaurants; up to ₹50 lakh for eligible service providers.
  2. Tax rates on turnover: 1% for manufacturers and traders (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST), 5% for restaurants not serving alcohol, 6% for service providers.
  3. Restrictions: can't collect tax from customers (issue a Bill of Supply), can't claim ITC, can't make inter-state outward supplies of goods or sell through most e-commerce operators, and must display "composition taxable person" on signboards and bills.
  4. Returns: CMP-08 quarterly statement-cum-challan and GSTR-4 annual return.
  5. In TallyPrime, set registration type Composition in GST details; sales print as Bills of Supply and the composition tax is computed on turnover.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Topic Key rule RCM payer Recipient RCM payment Cash only; ITC claimable if eligible Self-invoice For purchases from unregistered under RCM GSTR-3B 3.1(d) liability, 4 ITC Composition limit ₹1.5 crore (goods), ₹50 lakh (services) Composition rates 1% / 5% / 6% Composition returns CMP-08 quarterly, GSTR-4 annual

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: RCM shifts the tax obligation to the recipient where collecting from many small or unregistered suppliers would be impractical; requiring cash payment ensures real revenue enters the system before the recipient claims credit. The Composition Scheme trades simplicity for limits: low tax on turnover with minimal compliance, but no credit chain — which makes composition dealers less attractive suppliers for businesses that want ITC, a real commercial consideration when choosing the scheme.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Record for Godavari Wholesale Mart: advocate fees ₹50,000 under RCM, GTA freight ₹12,000 under RCM at 5%, and rent ₹40,000 for a godown from an unregistered owner. Compute the RCM liability, the cash payable and the ITC claimable. Then calculate quarterly composition tax for a small trader with ₹28 lakh turnover in the quarter.

docs.title: 08 · Bill-wise Details: Receivables & Payables
docs.text: Knowing that customers owe ₹4 lakh in total isn't enough — you need to know which invoices are unpaid, how old they are, and who to chase. Bill-wise accounting in TallyPrime tracks every invoice and payment against it.

docs.title: 1. Enable and configure
docs.text:
1. F11 → Maintain Bill-wise details: Yes (and for non-trading accounts if you track loans or advances bill-wise).
  2. In each customer/supplier ledger, set Maintain balances bill-by-bill: Yes and a Default credit period (e.g. 30 days).
  3. Opening balances can be broken into individual bills with dates.

docs.title: 2. Reference types
docs.text:
1. New Ref — a new bill (each sales or purchase invoice).
  2. Agst Ref — payment or receipt against an existing bill.
  3. Advance — money received/paid before the invoice.
  4. On Account — payment not linked to a specific bill (use sparingly; reconcile later).
  5. When recording a receipt, TallyPrime shows pending bills — choose the bills being paid.

docs.title: 3. Worked example
docs.text:
1. Sale to Srinivasa Stores: Inv. GWM/060, ₹59,000, credit 30 days (New Ref).
  2. Sale: Inv. GWM/072, ₹35,400 (New Ref).
  3. Receipt ₹70,000 by NEFT: Agst Ref GWM/060 ₹59,000 and Agst Ref GWM/072 ₹11,000 → GWM/072 has ₹24,400 pending.
  4. Advance ₹20,000 from a new customer for an upcoming order (Advance) — later adjusted against the invoice. Note: GST on advances for services is payable when received; for goods, generally not.

docs.title: 4. Outstanding and ageing reports
docs.text:
1. Alt+G → Receivables (Bills Receivable) and Payables: pending bills with due dates and overdue days.
  2. Ledger outstanding: one party's pending bills — share as a statement.
  3. Ageing analysis (F6/configure periods): 0–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+ days — identify risky debts.
  4. Interest calculation can be configured for overdue bills (F11 → Activate Interest Calculation) and applied per party.
  5. Reminder letters: print or email outstanding statements and reminders to customers.

docs.title: 5. Using it in practice
docs.text:
1. Weekly collection list: top overdue customers, amounts, last contact.
  2. Supplier payment planning: pay by due date to keep credit terms (and meet GST's 180-day rule for ITC).
  3. Watch days sales outstanding (DSO) = receivables ÷ credit sales × days; rising DSO strains cash.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Concept Use New Ref New invoice Agst Ref Payment against a bill Advance Paid/received before invoice On Account Unlinked (reconcile later) Receivables / Payables Pending bills, overdue days Ageing 0–30 / 31–60 / 61–90 / 90+ DSO Receivables ÷ credit sales × days

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Without bill-wise tracking, a party ledger is just a running balance — payments can't be matched to invoices, so ageing and disputes become guesswork. Bill references create a link between each invoice and the receipts settling it, which lets TallyPrime compute exactly what's overdue and by how long. That information drives collections, credit decisions and compliance rules like the 180-day ITC condition on supplier payments.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Enable bill-wise details for Godavari Wholesale Mart. Record six invoices across three customers, two partial receipts with Agst Ref, one advance and one on-account receipt. Produce the Receivables and ageing reports, print one customer's outstanding statement and calculate DSO for the month.

docs.title: 09 · Cost Centres & Budgets
docs.text: Total profit tells you how the business did; cost centres tell you which branch, department, project or salesperson drove it. Budgets let you plan and compare actual results. This module sets up both.

docs.title: 1. Cost categories and centres
docs.text:
1. F11 → Maintain Cost Centres: Yes; enable Cost Categories if you need more than one dimension.
  2. Cost category = a dimension: "Branches", "Salespeople", "Projects".
  3. Cost centres under each: Branches → Vijayawada, Guntur, Rajahmundry; Salespeople → Ravi, Kiran.
  4. Create via Alt+G → Create Master → Cost Category / Cost Centre.

docs.title: 2. Allocate in vouchers
docs.text:
1. In ledgers you want to analyse (Sales, Rent, Salary, Freight, Advertising), set Cost centres are applicable: Yes.
  2. While entering a voucher, TallyPrime asks for allocation: e.g. Rent ₹45,000 → Vijayawada ₹25,000, Guntur ₹12,000, Rajahmundry ₹8,000.
  3. Sales can be allocated by branch and by salesperson in the same voucher (different categories).
  4. Use cost centre classes to apply a fixed allocation automatically (e.g. salary always split 50/30/20).

docs.title: 3. Cost centre reports
docs.text:
1. Alt+G → Cost Centre Break-up, Category Summary and Ledger break-up.
  2. Branch profitability: allocate sales and direct/indirect costs by branch to see each branch's contribution.
  3. Salesperson performance: sales value, margin and discounts by person.
  4. Drill down to vouchers to verify allocations.

docs.title: 4. Budgets
docs.text:
1. F11 → Maintain Budgets (Budgets and Controls in some releases), then Alt+G → Create Master → Budget.
  2. Name ("FY 2026-27 Plan"), period (1-4-2026 to 31-3-2027), and set budget amounts on groups, ledgers or cost centres: e.g. Indirect Expenses ₹18,00,000 for the year; Advertising ₹2,40,000; Sales target ₹3,00,00,000; Guntur branch expenses ₹4,00,000.
  3. Budget type: On closing balance, on nett transactions — choose net transactions for income/expense period totals.
  4. Compare in Trial Balance, Group Summary or Cost Centre reports by adding the budget column (F12 / Budget Variance): actual vs budget with variance and percentage.
  5. Review monthly; investigate variances above a threshold (e.g. ±10%).

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Feature Path Enable F11 → Cost Centres / Budgets Category Dimension (branch, person, project) Allocation In voucher, ledgers with cost centres applicable Classes Auto-allocation rules Reports Cost Centre Break-up, Category Summary Budget Create Master → Budget; variance in reports

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Cost centres add extra dimensions to each posting without changing the accounts: the same rent entry still hits the Rent ledger, but also carries tags for the branch it belongs to. Reports then slice the general ledger by those tags. Budgets are stored targets attached to groups, ledgers or centres for a period; variance reports subtract budget from actual, turning the books into a management tool that highlights where performance departs from plan.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Set up branch and salesperson cost categories for Godavari Wholesale Mart. Record five sales and four expenses with allocations, then produce branch-wise profitability. Create an annual budget for sales, advertising and rent by branch, and generate a budget variance report for the month.

docs.title: 10 · Project — A GST-Compliant Month for a Wholesaler
docs.text: Combine Level 2: run a full GST month for a wholesaler — setup, invoicing, notes, ITC reconciliation, RCM, e-documents, receivables and returns — in TallyPrime. Use a new company, Krishna Electricals, Pune (Maharashtra, GSTIN state code 27), regular taxpayer with monthly returns.

docs.title: 1. Setup
docs.text:
1. Create the company with GST, bill-wise details, cost centres (branches: Pune, Nashik) and inventory.
  2. Tax ledgers (input/output CGST, SGST, IGST), GST-applicable sales/purchase ledgers, RCM-applicable Legal Fees and GTA Freight ledgers.
  3. Parties: four customers (two Maharashtra registered, one Gujarat registered, one unregistered retail), three suppliers (one inter-state).
  4. Items with HSN codes and current rates: LED panels, MCB switches, copper wire coils, ceiling fans, extension boards (look up actual rates on the CBIC rate finder).

docs.title: 2. Transactions
docs.text:
1. Five purchases (one inter-state), with supplier invoice numbers.
  2. Eight sales: intra-state B2B, inter-state B2B, B2C retail, one inter-state B2C above ₹1 lakh; allocate to branches.
  3. One sales return credit note and one pre-agreed discount credit note.
  4. One purchase return.
  5. RCM: advocate fees ₹30,000 and GTA freight ₹8,000.
  6. Receipts: two full, one partial (Agst Ref), one advance; supplier payments within terms.
  7. Assume turnover above ₹5 crore: prepare e-invoice and e-way bill details for two B2B invoices.

docs.title: 3. Compliance
docs.text:
1. Reconcile purchases with a GSTR-2B you create (include one mismatch and one supplier non-filer).
  2. Generate GSTR-1; resolve uncertain transactions; export JSON.
  3. Prepare GSTR-3B; compute set-off in the correct order; record the set-off journal and the payment voucher (including RCM paid in cash).
  4. Produce Receivables ageing and branch-wise profitability.

docs.title: Deliverable checklist
docs.text: Item Done? Company + GST masters complete Purchases, sales, notes recorded RCM entries and self-invoices E-invoice/e-way bill details GSTR-2B reconciliation with actions GSTR-1 JSON + GSTR-3B with set-off Payment vouchers, receivables ageing, branch P&L

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: A GST month is a closed loop: every sale and purchase recorded with correct masters feeds the returns, the returns determine tax payable, reconciliation verifies credits against the portal, and payment entries bring the books back in line with the government's ledgers. When the loop is run carefully each month, annual returns and audits become routine — when it isn't, errors compound into notices, interest and lost credits.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Complete the month for Krishna Electricals and write a one-page compliance summary: output tax, eligible ITC, ITC held back (and why), RCM paid, cash tax paid by head (CGST/SGST/IGST), GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B status, and three issues to resolve before next month.

docs.title: Level 3 · Advanced Compliance & Operations
