docs.title: 01 · TDS: Deduction, Payment & Returns
docs.text:
Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) requires a payer to deduct income tax from certain payments — contractor bills, professional fees, rent, commission, salaries — and deposit it with the government. This module covers the main rules and recording TDS in TallyPrime.

2026 note: From 1 April 2026 the Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the Income-tax Act, 1961. TDS provisions are consolidated (largely in section 393) with new form numbers, while most rates and thresholds carried over. Many professionals — and many software screens — still refer to the familiar 1961-Act labels (194C, 194J…), which this lesson shows for clarity. Always confirm current rates, thresholds and forms on incometax.gov.in and in your TallyPrime release notes.

docs.title: 1. Common TDS categories (familiar labels)
docs.text:
Nature of payment Familiar section Rate (resident) Threshold (indicative) Contractors 194C 1% individual/HUF, 2% others ₹30,000 single / ₹1,00,000 in a year Professional fees 194J 10% ₹50,000 in a year Technical services, royalty (certain) 194J 2% ₹50,000 in a year Rent – land/building/furniture 194I 10% ₹50,000 per month Rent – plant/machinery 194I 2% ₹50,000 per month Commission/brokerage 194H 2% ₹20,000 in a year Purchase of goods (large buyers) 194Q 0.1% above ₹50 lakh Buyer turnover > ₹10 crore Salaries 192 Slab rates Above exemption
  1. If the payee doesn't provide a valid PAN, TDS generally applies at a higher rate (often 20%).
  2. Deduct at the time of credit to the payee's account or payment, whichever is earlier.

docs.title: 2. Deposit, returns and certificates
docs.text:
1. Deposit TDS by the 7th of the following month (for March, by 30 April) through the challan on the income tax portal.
  2. File quarterly TDS statements (salary and non-salary; separate statements for non-residents) by 31 July, 31 October, 31 January and 31 May.
  3. Issue TDS certificates to payees (quarterly for non-salary, annually for salary employees) from the TRACES portal.
  4. Interest applies on late deduction/deposit and fees on late statements.
  5. You need a TAN (Tax Deduction Account Number) to deduct TDS.

docs.title: 3. TDS in TallyPrime
docs.text:
1. F11 → Enable Tax Deducted at Source (TDS); enter TAN, deductor type and responsible person details.
  2. Create TDS nature of payment masters (TallyPrime includes standard ones) with rates and thresholds.
  3. Create a TDS payable ledger under Duties & Taxes (Type: TDS), linked to the nature of payment.
  4. In party ledgers (e.g. "Sharma Contractors"), set Is TDS deductable: Yes, deductee type (Individual/Company) and PAN.
  5. In expense ledgers (e.g. "Contract Charges"), set TDS applicable with the nature of payment.

docs.title: 4. Worked example
docs.text:
1. Contractor bill ₹1,20,000 (company contractor, 2%): Journal or Purchase voucher — Dr Contract Charges ₹1,20,000; Cr Sharma Contractors ₹1,17,600; Cr TDS Payable – Contractors ₹2,400. TallyPrime calculates the TDS once thresholds are crossed.
  2. Pay the contractor ₹1,17,600 (Payment voucher).
  3. Deposit TDS ₹2,400 by the 7th: Payment voucher using Stat Payment (Ctrl+F) to fill period and nature of payment, then record the challan details (BSR code, challan number, date).
  4. Generate TDS reports: Alt+G → TDS Reports — computation, challan reconciliation, return forms (export for the return preparation utility).

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Step Rule Deduct At credit or payment, whichever earlier No PAN Higher rate Deposit 7th of next month (30 April for March) Returns Quarterly: 31 Jul, 31 Oct, 31 Jan, 31 May Certificates From TRACES TallyPrime F11 TDS, nature of payment, party PAN, Stat Payment

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: TDS collects tax progressively at the point income is paid, rather than waiting for the recipient's annual return. The deductor acts as a collection agent: amounts deducted are linked to the payee's PAN through quarterly statements, appear in the payee's tax credit statement, and are credited against their final tax liability. That's why accurate PANs, correct categories and timely statements matter — errors leave payees without credit and expose the deductor to interest, fees and disallowance of the expense.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: For a manufacturing company, record: a contractor bill ₹1,20,000 (company, 2%), professional fees ₹75,000 to a CA, monthly office rent ₹80,000, and commission ₹25,000 to an agent without PAN. Calculate TDS for each, record vouchers and the deposit, and list the due date for deposit and for the quarterly statement.

docs.title: 02 · TCS & Other Withholdings
docs.text: While TDS is deducted by the payer, Tax Collected at Source (TCS) is collected by the seller from the buyer on specified transactions. GST also has its own TCS for e-commerce operators. This module covers both and how to record them. Rules are as of 2026 — confirm current provisions under the Income-tax Act, 2025 and GST law.

docs.title: 1. Income-tax TCS — common cases
docs.text:
1. Sale of specified goods: scrap (1%), alcoholic liquor for human consumption (1%), tendu leaves, timber and forest produce, minerals (coal, lignite, iron ore) at notified rates.
  2. Sale of a motor vehicle above ₹10 lakh (1%), and from 2025 certain notified luxury goods above ₹10 lakh.
  3. Foreign remittances under LRS and overseas tour packages: TCS above thresholds (e.g. 20% on certain LRS remittances above ₹10 lakh; lower or nil for education funded by loans and medical purposes).
  4. The earlier general TCS on sale of goods above ₹50 lakh was withdrawn from April 2025 (TDS on purchase of goods by large buyers continues).
  5. Collect at the time of receipt or debit to the buyer, deposit by the 7th of the following month, file quarterly TCS statements and issue certificates.
  6. The seller needs a TAN; buyers without PAN face higher rates.

docs.title: 2. TCS in TallyPrime
docs.text:
1. F11 → Enable Tax Collected at Source (TCS) with TAN and collector details.
  2. Create a TCS payable ledger under Duties & Taxes (Type: TCS) with the nature of goods.
  3. Set TCS applicability in the buyer's ledger (PAN, collectee type) and in the sales ledger or stock item (nature of goods).
  4. Example: sale of scrap ₹2,00,000 + GST 18% (₹36,000) = ₹2,36,000; TCS 1% on the sale value as per current rules → TallyPrime adds the TCS line to the invoice and the buyer pays the invoice plus TCS.
  5. Deposit with Stat Payment; generate TCS reports and return data from Alt+G → TCS Reports.

docs.title: 3. GST TCS for e-commerce
docs.text:
1. E-commerce operators (Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho and others) collect GST TCS of 0.5% (0.25% CGST + 0.25% SGST, or 0.5% IGST) on net taxable supplies made through their platforms by sellers, under section 52 of the CGST Act.
  2. Operators report it monthly in GSTR-8; the amount appears in the seller's electronic cash ledger after the seller accepts it, and can be used to pay GST.
  3. In TallyPrime, record marketplace settlements: sales at gross value, marketplace commission (with GST, as an expense with ITC), GST TCS (as a receivable/asset ledger until claimed) and income-tax TDS deducted by the operator under the e-commerce provisions (0.1%), then the net bank receipt.

docs.title: 4. Reconcile marketplace payments
docs.text:
1. Download settlement reports from the seller portal.
  2. Match orders, returns, commissions, shipping fees, TCS and TDS to your books.
  3. Reconcile GST TCS with GSTR-2B/TCS credit and accept it on the portal.
  4. Claim income-tax TDS through your tax credit statement (Form 26AS/AIS).

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Withholding Who collects Rate (examples) Report Income-tax TCS Seller Scrap 1%, motor vehicle > ₹10 lakh 1% Quarterly TCS statement LRS TCS Bank/forex dealer 20% above ₹10 lakh (certain purposes) — GST TCS E-commerce operator 0.5% GSTR-8 E-commerce TDS (income tax) Operator 0.1% Operator's TDS return

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: TCS places the collection obligation on the party best placed to identify the transaction — sellers of specified goods, banks handling remittances, marketplaces handling sales — creating a trail that ties transactions to taxpayers' PANs and GSTINs. Collected amounts become credits for the payer or seller in their own tax accounts, so recording them as receivable assets (not expenses) and reconciling them with government statements ensures the business actually uses those credits.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Record a scrap sale with GST and income-tax TCS for a buyer with PAN and for one without PAN. Then record a monthly Flipkart settlement for a seller: gross sales ₹3,00,000 including GST, returns ₹20,000, commission ₹36,000 + GST, shipping fees ₹12,000 + GST, GST TCS and TDS, and the net bank receipt. Show the journal and the reconciliation.

docs.title: 03 · Payroll: Salary, PF & ESI
docs.text: TallyPrime has a built-in payroll module that calculates salaries, statutory deductions and generates payslips and compliance reports. This module sets up payroll for a small company. Statutory rates are as of 2026; the new labour codes (in force from November 2025, with rules being notified) may change wage definitions and contributions — confirm with current EPFO/ESIC notifications.

docs.title: 1. Statutory basics
docs.text:
1. Provident Fund (EPF): applies to establishments with 20+ employees (voluntary below). Employee contributes 12% of basic + DA; employer contributes 12%, of which 8.33% (capped on ₹15,000 wages = ₹1,250/month) goes to the pension scheme (EPS) and the rest to EPF. Employer also pays admin charges (0.5%) and EDLI (0.5%). Mandatory coverage for wages up to ₹15,000 (higher-wage employees can be covered).
  2. ESI: applies to establishments with 10+ employees (in notified areas) for employees earning up to ₹21,000 a month. Employee 0.75%, employer 3.25% of gross wages.
  3. Professional tax: state-specific (e.g. Maharashtra up to ₹200/month with ₹300 in February; Karnataka ₹200 for salaries above a threshold); some states don't levy it.
  4. TDS on salary: deducted monthly based on estimated annual tax under the regime the employee chooses (the new regime is the default).
  5. Labour Welfare Fund and gratuity/bonus obligations may also apply.

docs.title: 2. Payroll setup in TallyPrime
docs.text:
1. F11 → Maintain Payroll: Yes; enable statutory features (PF, ESI, PT, Income Tax) and enter registration numbers.
  2. Create employee groups (Office, Sales, Factory) and employees with joining date, designation, PAN, UAN, ESI number, bank account.
  3. Create attendance/production types: Present, Absent, Leave, Overtime hours.
  4. Create pay heads: Basic (earnings, on attendance), HRA (% of basic), Conveyance (flat), Special Allowance, Overtime (rate per hour), PF Employee (deduction), ESI Employee, Professional Tax, TDS on Salary; employer contributions PF and ESI.
  5. Define salary details for each employee or group with effective dates.

docs.title: 3. Monthly processing
docs.text:
1. Record Attendance voucher (Ctrl+F5) — days present, leave, overtime.
  2. Process the Payroll voucher (Ctrl+F4 → Payroll Auto Fill): TallyPrime calculates earnings, deductions and net pay.
  3. Example — Priya, basic ₹14,000, HRA ₹5,600, special ₹2,400 (gross ₹22,000):
  4. PF employee 12% × 14,000 = ₹1,680; employer ₹1,680 (EPS ₹1,166, EPF ₹514).
  5. ESI not applicable (gross above ₹21,000).
  6. Professional tax ₹200 → net pay ₹20,120 (before any TDS).
  7. Record the salary payment (Payment voucher or bank transfer file) and the employer contribution journal.
  8. Pay PF and ESI by the 15th of the following month (ECR filing on the EPFO portal; ESI on the ESIC portal).

docs.title: 4. Payroll reports
docs.text:
1. Payslips (print/email), Pay Sheet, Attendance Sheet, Payment Advice for the bank.
  2. Statutory reports: PF ECR, ESI monthly contribution, PT computation, Form 16 data for TDS.
  3. Gratuity computation and leave encashment reports where configured.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Item Rule (2026) PF 12% employee + 12% employer (8.33% EPS capped at ₹1,250) PF wage ceiling ₹15,000 (mandatory) ESI 0.75% employee + 3.25% employer, wages ≤ ₹21,000 PF/ESI due 15th of next month Payroll voucher Ctrl+F4 Attendance Ctrl+F5

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Payroll in TallyPrime separates what each employee earns (salary structure built from pay heads with formulas) from how much they worked (attendance), then computes statutory deductions using configured rules and ceilings. Payroll vouchers post directly to salary expense, liability and statutory payable ledgers, so payroll costs flow into the P&L and the statutory dues sit as liabilities until paid — making compliance due dates visible in the books.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Set up payroll for five employees with different salaries (two below ₹21,000 gross for ESI). Create pay heads with formulas, record one month's attendance, process payroll, and generate payslips, the pay sheet and PF/ESI reports. Calculate the total employer cost for the month.

docs.title: 04 · Advanced Inventory: Batches, Godowns & Valuation
docs.text: As stock grows, you need to know where items are, which batch they came from (for expiry or quality), and how stock is valued. This module covers godowns, batches, valuation methods and stock controls in TallyPrime.

docs.title: 1. Godowns (locations)
docs.text:
1. F11 → Maintain Multiple Godowns: Yes.
  2. Create godowns: Main Warehouse, Retail Counter, Nashik Depot, Damaged Stock (with "Our stock with third party" or "Third party stock with us" options for consignment and job work).
  3. Every item-based voucher asks for the godown; opening stock can be split by godown.
  4. Transfer stock with a Stock Journal (Alt+F7) → Transfer (e.g. 100 fans from Main Warehouse to Nashik Depot) or use a Material In/Out voucher for job work.
  5. Godown Summary report shows stock by location.

docs.title: 2. Batches, expiry and serial numbers
docs.text:
1. F11 → Enable Batches (and Expiry Dates for medicines, food, chemicals).
  2. In the stock item, set Maintain in batches: Yes, track date of manufacture and use expiry dates.
  3. Enter batch number, manufacturing and expiry dates on purchase; select batches on sale (FEFO — first expiry, first out — for perishables).
  4. Batch-wise reports and ageing analysis reveal slow-moving or near-expiry stock.

docs.title: 3. Valuation methods
docs.text:
1. Set per stock item under Costing method: Average Cost (default), FIFO, Last Purchase Cost, Standard Cost, etc.; and Market valuation method for reports.
  2. Example — copper wire coils:
  3. Opening 100 @ ₹1,800; purchase 200 @ ₹1,950; sold 220.
  4. FIFO: 100 @ 1,800 + 120 @ 1,950 = ₹4,14,000 COGS; closing 80 @ 1,950 = ₹1,56,000.
  5. Weighted average: (1,80,000 + 3,90,000) ÷ 300 = ₹1,900; COGS 220 × 1,900 = ₹4,18,000; closing 80 × 1,900 = ₹1,52,000.
  6. Accounting standards require inventory at the lower of cost and net realisable value; choose a method consistently and disclose it.

docs.title: 4. Stock controls
docs.text:
1. Reorder levels and minimum order quantities per item/godown → Reorder Status report suggests purchases.
  2. Negative stock warnings (F12) prevent selling stock you don't have.
  3. Physical Stock voucher (Ctrl+F7) after counts; investigate differences before adjusting.
  4. Price levels (F11 → Multiple price levels) for wholesale, retail and dealer prices.
  5. Additional cost of purchase (freight, insurance) can be loaded into item cost for accurate valuation.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Feature Use Godowns Stock by location, transfers Batches & expiry Traceability, FEFO Costing method Average, FIFO, last purchase Reorder levels Automated purchase suggestions Negative stock warning Prevent overselling Price levels Different selling prices

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Each item movement records quantity, godown, batch and value. TallyPrime computes cost of goods sold and closing stock by replaying movements under the item's costing method — FIFO consumes the oldest cost layers first, while average cost blends them. Because closing stock directly affects profit, the method you choose changes reported profit when prices rise or fall, which is why consistency and documentation are required by accounting standards and auditors.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Enable godowns and batches for Krishna Electricals. Create three godowns, record purchases in batches across godowns, transfer stock between them, and sell using batch selection. Compute COGS and closing stock for the copper wire example under FIFO and average cost, set it in TallyPrime, and compare the Stock Summary under both methods.

docs.title: 05 · Manufacturing: Bill of Materials & Job Work
docs.text: Manufacturers turn raw materials into finished goods. TallyPrime records this with a Bill of Materials (BOM) and manufacturing journals, and handles job work — sending materials to others for processing, or processing for others. Our example: Deccan Furniture Works makes study tables.

docs.title: 1. Set up a Bill of Materials
docs.text:
1. In the finished stock item "Study Table – Standard", set Set components (BoM): Yes.
  2. Define components per 1 unit: Plywood sheet 1 No, Teak legs 4 Nos, Screws 32 Nos, Laminate 1.5 sq m, Drawer runners 1 set; optional scrap/by-product: wood waste 0.5 kg.
  3. Specify godowns for components and output, and multiple BOMs if there are variants.
  4. Raw materials are separate stock items with their own costs and GST details.

docs.title: 2. Record production
docs.text:
1. Use Stock Journal (Alt+F7) → Manufacture (or a Manufacturing Journal voucher type).
  2. Select the finished item and quantity (e.g. 20 tables); TallyPrime fills components from the BOM (20 plywood sheets, 80 legs, 640 screws, 30 sq m laminate, 20 runner sets).
  3. Add additional costs of manufacturing — direct labour ₹12,000, power ₹3,000 — so the finished goods cost includes them.
  4. Finished goods cost per table = (components + additional costs) ÷ 20.
  5. Stock of raw materials decreases and finished goods increases; accounts reflect values through stock valuation.

docs.title: 3. Job work — sending materials out (principal)
docs.text:
1. F11 → Enable Job Order Processing.
  2. Create a Job Work Out Order to the job worker (e.g. polishing unit), then Material Out voucher to send tables for polishing.
  3. Record Material In when polished goods return, and the job worker's purchase invoice for processing charges (with GST).
  4. Under GST, goods sent for job work move on a delivery challan without tax; inputs must return within 1 year and capital goods within 3 years, or they're treated as supplies.
  5. Report job work movements in the ITC-04 form (annual or half-yearly depending on turnover, as currently applicable).

docs.title: 4. Job work — processing for others (job worker)
docs.text:
1. Create a Job Work In Order from the principal.
  2. Material In records the principal's goods received (tracked as third-party stock, not yours).
  3. Record consumption and Material Out when returning processed goods.
  4. Raise a sales invoice for job work charges (services, with applicable GST rate and SAC).

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Task Voucher Define recipe BoM in stock item Production Stock Journal → Manufacture Add labour/overheads Additional cost in manufacture Send to job worker Job Work Out Order → Material Out Receive back Material In + job worker invoice Process for others Job Work In Order → Material In/Out GST report ITC-04

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: A BOM is a recipe that tells TallyPrime how much of each input one unit of output consumes, so a single manufacture entry moves dozens of stock quantities consistently. The finished item's cost is built from component costs plus loaded overheads, which feeds inventory valuation and gross margin. Job work tracking keeps ownership clear — materials at a job worker remain the principal's stock — which matters for valuation, insurance and the GST rules that allow tax-free movement only within time limits.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Create raw materials and a BOM for a study table, record opening raw material stock, manufacture 20 tables with labour and power costs, and compute the cost per table. Then send 10 tables to a polishing job worker, receive them back, and record the job worker's invoice with GST.

docs.title: 06 · Banking: Cheques, e-Payments & Post-Dated Cheques
docs.text: TallyPrime includes banking utilities that save time and reduce errors: cheque printing, cheque registers, e-payment files, post-dated cheque management and deposit slips. This module covers the ones most businesses use.

docs.title: 1. Cheque printing and register
docs.text:
1. Enable cheque printing in the bank ledger (Set cheque books: Yes; cheque range; cheque printing configuration for your bank's format).
  2. TallyPrime provides formats for many Indian banks; adjust dimensions in Cheque Printing Configuration if needed.
  3. In a Payment voucher from that bank, choose transaction type Cheque — TallyPrime picks the next cheque number and prints the cheque with amount in words.
  4. Cheque Register (Alt+G → Cheque Register) shows issued, blank, cancelled and unused cheques; mark cancelled cheques with reasons.
  5. Cheque Management tracks cheques deposited and their clearing status.

docs.title: 2. e-Payments
docs.text:
1. Enable e-Payments in the bank ledger (supported banks) and fill beneficiary bank details (account number, IFSC) in party ledgers.
  2. Record Payment vouchers with transaction type e-Fund Transfer (NEFT/RTGS/IMPS).
  3. Open Banking → e-Payments report, select payments and export the bank-specific payment file for upload on your net banking portal (or use direct connected banking where supported).
  4. After the bank processes payments, update the status and UTR numbers; the entries flow into bank reconciliation.
  5. Apply maker-checker controls: one person creates, another approves uploads in net banking.

docs.title: 3. Post-dated cheques (PDCs)
docs.text:
1. A PDC is a cheque dated in the future — common for rent, EMIs and customer instalments.
  2. In TallyPrime, record the voucher with the future date and mark it Post-Dated (voucher setting); it doesn't affect balances until that date.
  3. Post-Dated Summary (Alt+G → Post-Dated Vouchers) lists upcoming receipts and payments — useful for cash flow forecasting.
  4. On the due date, the voucher becomes regular automatically; deposit or present the cheque and reconcile.

docs.title: 4. Deposit slips and payment advice
docs.text:
1. Deposit Slip report generates a list of cheques/cash to deposit — print and take to the bank.
  2. Payment Advice sends parties details of payments made (invoices settled, TDS deducted).
  3. Email advice directly with Alt+M.

docs.title: 5. Dishonoured cheques
docs.text:
1. If a customer's cheque bounces, record a reversal: Dr Customer / Cr Bank, plus bank charges (Dr Bank Charges / Cr Bank) and optionally recover charges from the customer.
  2. Mark the original cheque as dishonoured in cheque management for tracking.
  3. Note legal timelines under the Negotiable Instruments Act if you plan to act on a dishonoured cheque.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Utility Purpose Cheque printing Print cheques from payment vouchers Cheque Register Track cheque numbers and status e-Payments Export NEFT/RTGS bank files Post-Dated Summary Upcoming cheques for cash planning Deposit Slip Bank deposit list Payment Advice Inform parties of payments

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Banking utilities read the same payment and receipt vouchers that drive your books, adding instrument details (cheque numbers, UTRs, dates) that the bank also records. Because both sides share identifiers, reconciliation becomes largely automatic. Post-dated vouchers sit outside current balances until their date, giving you a forward view of committed cash flows without distorting today's books.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Configure cheque printing for your bank ledger, issue two cheque payments and cancel one cheque. Record three NEFT supplier payments and generate the e-payment file. Record two post-dated receipts from customers, view the Post-Dated Summary, and record one dishonoured cheque with bank charges.

docs.title: 07 · Foreign Currency & Exports
docs.text: Businesses that export, import or have foreign customers deal with multiple currencies and exchange rate changes. TallyPrime handles foreign currency transactions and forex gains/losses, while GST treats exports as zero-rated. This module covers both.

docs.title: 1. Enable multiple currencies
docs.text:
1. F11 → Allow Multi-Currency: Yes.
  2. Create currencies: USD ($), EUR (€), AED (د.إ) with symbols and decimal places.
  3. Set Rates of Exchange (Alt+G → Rates of Exchange) — standard rate, selling and buying rates for dates.
  4. In foreign party ledgers (e.g. "Global Home Goods LLC, USA"), set currency USD and registration type Overseas.

docs.title: 2. Export invoice
docs.text:
1. Sale to a US customer: 500 ceiling fans @ $28 = $14,000, exchange rate ₹84.50 → ₹11,83,000.
  2. In the sales invoice, select the foreign ledger; enter rates in USD; TallyPrime converts using the rate.
  3. Add export details: port code, shipping bill number and date (for GST reporting).
  4. GST treatment (zero-rated supply):
  5. Under LUT (Letter of Undertaking filed annually on the GST portal): export without paying IGST, then claim refund of unutilised ITC; or
  6. With payment of IGST, then claim refund of IGST paid (automatically processed via shipping bill data for goods).
  7. Exports of services must meet conditions (recipient outside India, payment in convertible foreign exchange or permitted INR, etc.).

docs.title: 3. Receipts and forex gain/loss
docs.text:
1. Customer pays $14,000 when the rate is ₹85.10 → bank receives ₹11,91,400.
  2. Record the receipt in USD against the invoice; TallyPrime computes the exchange gain of ₹8,400 (14,000 × 0.60).
  3. Book it with a forex gain/loss adjustment (Journal: Dr Customer / Cr Forex Gain, under Indirect Incomes), or let TallyPrime's forex adjustment feature post it.
  4. At year-end, restate open foreign currency balances at the closing rate and book unrealised gain/loss (the Forex Gain/Loss report helps).

docs.title: 4. Imports
docs.text:
1. Purchase from a Chinese supplier in USD; record import duty (customs) and IGST on imports paid at customs per the Bill of Entry.
  2. IGST on imports is claimable as ITC (it appears in GSTR-2B from customs data).
  3. Customs duty becomes part of the inventory cost.
  4. Import of services: pay IGST under reverse charge (Module 7 of Level 2).

docs.title: 5. Compliance reminders
docs.text:
1. Export proceeds must be realised within RBI's prescribed period (currently up to 15 months for goods exports, subject to updates); banks report realisation through the EDPMS system.
  2. Keep shipping bills, bills of entry, bank realisation certificates (e-BRC) and LUT copies.
  3. GSTR-1 reports exports in Table 6A; refunds are claimed on the portal.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Item Treatment Currency setup F11 multi-currency, rates of exchange Export under LUT No IGST; refund ITC Export with IGST Pay IGST; refund Forex gain/loss Realised on receipt; restate at year-end Import IGST Paid at customs; claim ITC Customs duty Added to inventory cost

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Foreign currency transactions are recorded at the exchange rate on the transaction date, but settled later at a different rate; the difference is a real gain or loss that must be recognised. TallyPrime tracks the original foreign amount alongside rupee values, so it can compute gains on settlement and restate open balances at the year-end rate. GST zero-rates exports so that Indian goods and services compete internationally without carrying domestic tax, with refunds ensuring input taxes don't become a cost.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Enable multi-currency for Krishna Electricals. docs.title: 08 · Year-End Adjustments: Depreciation & Provisions
docs.text: Before closing a financial year, accountants post adjusting entries so the accounts reflect the true profit and position: depreciation, outstanding and prepaid expenses, accrued income, provisions and closing stock checks. This module walks through them in TallyPrime.

docs.title: 1. Depreciation
docs.text:
1. Companies Act (Schedule II) uses useful lives (e.g. furniture 10 years, computers 3 years, plant and machinery 15 years) with straight-line or written-down value; income-tax depreciation uses block-wise WDV rates (e.g. 10% furniture, 15% plant and machinery, 40% computers) with half-rate for assets used under 180 days in the year. The two often differ — book depreciation goes in the accounts; tax depreciation goes in the tax computation.
  2. Example (book, WDV for illustration): Furniture opening WDV ₹2,40,000 at 10% → ₹24,000. Computer bought 1 October for ₹90,000; on income-tax rules, 40% × half year → ₹18,000.
  3. TallyPrime entry (Journal): Dr Depreciation (Indirect Expenses) / Cr Furniture, Cr Computer.
  4. Maintain a fixed asset register (TallyPrime's fixed asset features or a spreadsheet) with cost, additions, disposals and depreciation by asset.

docs.title: 2. Outstanding, prepaid and accrued items
docs.text:
1. Outstanding expenses (incurred, not paid): March electricity ₹14,000 → Dr Electricity / Cr Outstanding Expenses (Current Liabilities).
  2. Prepaid expenses (paid in advance): insurance ₹36,000 paid for July–June → 3 months (April–June next year) prepaid ₹9,000 → Dr Prepaid Insurance (Current Assets) / Cr Insurance.
  3. Accrued income (earned, not received): interest on FD ₹6,500 → Dr Accrued Interest / Cr Interest Received.
  4. Income received in advance: Dr Income / Cr Advance Income (liability).
  5. Use reversing journals (optional voucher class) at the start of the next year where appropriate.

docs.title: 3. Provisions
docs.text:
1. Provision for doubtful debts: estimate unrecoverable receivables (from the ageing report): e.g. 5% of debts over 90 days ₹3,20,000 → ₹16,000: Dr Bad Debts / Provision Expense / Cr Provision for Doubtful Debts.
  2. Bad debts written off: Dr Bad Debts / Cr Customer (with GST considerations — output tax already paid isn't automatically recoverable).
  3. Provision for income tax and gratuity/leave (based on estimates or actuarial valuation for larger companies).
  4. Provision for warranty if products carry warranties.

docs.title: 4. Stock and other checks
docs.text:
1. Physical stock verification, write down damaged or obsolete stock to net realisable value.
  2. Confirm balances with major customers and suppliers; reconcile all bank accounts.
  3. Review GST: ITC reversals for unpaid suppliers (180 days), blocked credits, and match books to GSTR-3B for the year.
  4. Review TDS: all deductions deposited and returns filed.
  5. After adjustments, the year can be closed: TallyPrime carries balances forward automatically when you start entering in the new year (or split the company — Level 4).

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Adjustment Entry Depreciation Dr Depreciation / Cr Asset Outstanding expense Dr Expense / Cr Outstanding (liability) Prepaid expense Dr Prepaid (asset) / Cr Expense Accrued income Dr Accrued (asset) / Cr Income Doubtful debts Dr Provision expense / Cr Provision Stock write-down Value at lower of cost and NRV

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Accounts are prepared on an accrual basis: income and expenses belong to the period in which they're earned or incurred, not when cash moves. Year-end adjustments move amounts into the right period and recognise the consumption of long-lived assets through depreciation, so profit reflects the year's real economic performance. Provisions apply prudence — recognising probable losses as soon as they can be estimated — which protects users of the accounts from overstated profits.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: For Krishna Electricals at 31 March, post: depreciation on furniture and a computer bought in October (book and note tax depreciation), outstanding electricity and salary, prepaid insurance, accrued FD interest, a 5% provision on debts over 90 days and a stock write-down of ₹22,000. Compare the P&L before and after the adjustments.

docs.title: 09 · GSTR-9 Annual Return & Audit Readiness
docs.text: The GST year ends with the annual return (GSTR-9) and, for larger taxpayers, the reconciliation statement (GSTR-9C). This module prepares both and builds the documentation that keeps audits and departmental notices manageable. Thresholds as of 2026 — check current notifications.

docs.title: 1. Who files what
docs.text:
1. GSTR-9: regular taxpayers file annually by 31 December following the financial year. Filing is currently optional for taxpayers with aggregate turnover up to ₹2 crore.
  2. GSTR-9C (self-certified reconciliation between audited financial statements and GSTR-9): required for taxpayers with aggregate turnover above ₹5 crore.
  3. Composition taxpayers file GSTR-4; e-commerce operators GSTR-9B; others have specific forms.

docs.title: 2. GSTR-9 structure
docs.text:
1. Part II — outward and inward supplies declared during the year (from GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B).
  2. Part III — ITC availed (from GSTR-3B), split into inputs, capital goods, input services; ITC reversed; ITC as per GSTR-2B (Table 8 comparison).
  3. Part IV — tax paid as declared.
  4. Part V — transactions of the year declared in the next year's returns (up to the cut-off), amendments.
  5. Part VI — other info: demands/refunds, HSN-wise summary of outward and inward supplies, late fee.
  6. Many fields are auto-populated on the portal; you review, reconcile and explain differences.

docs.title: 3. Prepare in TallyPrime
docs.text:
1. Alt+G → GSTR-9 (or annual computation report) for the year.
  2. Compare TallyPrime's annual figures with the portal's auto-populated GSTR-9 and with the sum of filed GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B.
  3. Common differences: invoices missed in GSTR-1 but included in GSTR-3B, credit notes, wrong tax heads (CGST/SGST vs IGST), ITC claimed vs available in GSTR-2B, ITC reversals.
  4. Pay any additional liability discovered (with interest) through DRC-03 before filing.
  5. Export data and file on the portal with DSC/EVC.

docs.title: 4. Audit readiness
docs.text:
1. Monthly discipline prevents year-end surprises: GSTR-2B reconciliation, books vs returns comparison, prompt credit notes.
  2. Maintain records for at least 72 months from the due date of the annual return: invoices, credit/debit notes, e-way bills, delivery challans, ITC documents, payment proofs.
  3. Keep a reconciliation pack: turnover per books vs GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B vs e-invoices vs e-way bills; ITC per books vs GSTR-2B vs GSTR-3B.
  4. Respond to portal notices (e.g. ASMT-10 scrutiny, DRC-01 demands) within deadlines with reconciliations and documents.
  5. Use TallyPrime's edit log (Level 4) to show the history of changes to vouchers if questioned.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Return Who Due GSTR-9 Regular taxpayers (optional ≤ ₹2 crore) 31 Dec GSTR-9C AATO > ₹5 crore With GSTR-9 DRC-03 Voluntary payment of additional tax Before filing Records Retain 72 months Reconciliation pack Books vs returns vs portal Annual (monthly better)

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: GSTR-9 consolidates a year of monthly declarations so the tax department can compare them with each other, with suppliers' data and — via GSTR-9C — with audited financial statements. Differences that slipped through monthly returns surface here, which is why the annual return often triggers corrections, additional payments or notices. A business that reconciles monthly turns the annual return into a summary of already-verified figures.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Build an annual reconciliation for Krishna Electricals with assumed figures: turnover per books, per GSTR-1 and per GSTR-3B; ITC per books, GSTR-2B and GSTR-3B. Identify three differences, explain each, compute any additional tax with interest, and draft the corresponding GSTR-9 tables.

docs.title: 10 · Project — Quarter-End Close for a Manufacturer
docs.text: Combine Level 3 in a quarter-end close for Deccan Furniture Works (Hyderabad, Telangana) — manufacturing, payroll, TDS/TCS, inventory, banking, exports and adjustments — and produce management-ready reports.

docs.title: 1. Setup
docs.text:
1. Company with GST, TDS, TCS, payroll, multi-currency, godowns (Raw Materials Store, Factory Floor, Finished Goods, Showroom), batches for laminates, cost centres (Production, Sales, Admin).
  2. Raw materials, finished items with BOMs (study table, wardrobe, bookshelf), opening stock.
  3. Employees (6) with PF, ESI and PT; TDS natures of payment; TCS for scrap sales.

docs.title: 2. Transactions for the quarter
docs.text:
1. Purchases of raw materials (including an inter-state supplier and an import in USD with customs duty and import IGST).
  2. Production runs for all three products with labour and power as additional costs.
  3. Job work: tables sent for polishing and received back with the job worker's invoice.
  4. Sales: domestic B2B and B2C, one export under LUT in USD, scrap sale with TCS.
  5. Payroll for three months with attendance, PF/ESI payments by the 15th.
  6. TDS on contractor, professional fees and rent; deposits by the 7th; quarterly statement data.
  7. Banking: cheques, e-payments, two post-dated receipts, one dishonoured cheque.
  8. Forex receipt for the export at a different rate.

docs.title: 3. Close and report
docs.text:
1. Quarter-end adjustments: depreciation, outstanding expenses, prepaid items, provision for doubtful debts.
  2. Physical stock verification and adjustments; batch expiry review.
  3. Bank reconciliation for all accounts.
  4. GST: monthly GSTR-1/3B for the quarter, GSTR-2B reconciliation, ITC-04 data for job work.
  5. Reports: Trial Balance, P&L (with gross margin), Balance Sheet, Stock Summary by godown, Cost Centre break-up, payroll summary, TDS/TCS summary, forex gain/loss.

docs.title: Deliverable checklist
docs.text: Item Done? Manufacturing with BOM and additional costs Job work cycle Payroll 3 months + statutory payments TDS/TCS entries, deposits, return data Export, import, forex Adjustments + stock verification GST returns + reconciliations Management report pack

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: A quarter-end close tests whether all modules agree with each other: production consumption with stock counts, payroll costs with statutory dues, sales with GST returns and receivables, bank entries with statements. Accountants close in a fixed order — record, reconcile, adjust, review, report — because each step depends on the accuracy of the one before. Delivering this pack is close to what a finance team does every quarter in a real manufacturing company.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Complete the close and write a two-page management report: revenue by channel (domestic, export), gross margin by product, payroll cost as a percentage of revenue, cash position and upcoming post-dated receipts, statutory payments made and due, and three operational recommendations.

1. Financial Statement Analysis & Ratios

docs.title: 01 · Financial Statement Analysis & Ratios
docs.text: Recording transactions is half the job; interpreting them is where accountants add real value. This module uses ratios to judge a business's profitability, liquidity, efficiency and solvency, with TallyPrime's Ratio Analysis report.

docs.title: 1. Read the statements first
docs.text:
1. P&L: revenue growth, gross margin, operating expenses, net profit.
  2. Balance Sheet: working capital (current assets − current liabilities), debt, equity.
  3. Cash flow (Alt+G → Cash Flow / Funds Flow): cash from operations vs profit — profitable businesses can still run out of cash.
  4. Compare periods (add columns with Alt+C) and against budget.

docs.title: 2. Key ratios (worked example)
docs.text:
Sample figures for a trading company (₹ lakh): Sales 600, COGS 450, Operating expenses 96, Net profit 36, Current assets 180 (stock 90, debtors 75, cash 15), Current liabilities 110, Creditors 60, Equity 150, Debt 80, Purchases 470.

Ratio Formula Result Gross profit margin (Sales − COGS) ÷ Sales 150 ÷ 600 = 25% Net profit margin Net profit ÷ Sales 36 ÷ 600 = 6% Current ratio Current assets ÷ Current liabilities 180 ÷ 110 = 1.64 Quick ratio (Current assets − Stock) ÷ CL 90 ÷ 110 = 0.82 Debtor days (DSO) Debtors ÷ Sales × 365 75 ÷ 600 × 365 ≈ 46 days Inventory days Stock ÷ COGS × 365 90 ÷ 450 × 365 = 73 days Creditor days Creditors ÷ Purchases × 365 60 ÷ 470 × 365 ≈ 47 days Cash conversion cycle DSO + Inventory days − Creditor days 46 + 73 − 47 = 72 days Debt-to-equity Debt ÷ Equity 80 ÷ 150 = 0.53 Return on equity Net profit ÷ Equity 36 ÷ 150 = 24%

docs.title: 3. Interpret, don't just calculate
docs.text:
1. A quick ratio below 1 means the business depends on selling stock to pay short-term debts.
  2. A 72-day cash conversion cycle means each rupee of sales is tied up for over two months — reducing inventory days by 20 would free significant cash.
  3. Compare with industry norms and the business's own history; ratios mean little in isolation.
  4. Look for causes behind changes: falling gross margin could be price pressure, a product mix shift or purchase cost increases.

docs.title: 4. TallyPrime's Ratio Analysis
docs.text:
1. Alt+G → Ratio Analysis shows principal groups (working capital, cash, debtors, creditors, stock, sales, gross and net profit) and ratios (current ratio, quick ratio, debt/equity, gross and net profit %, return on investment, receivables turnover in days, inventory turnover).
  2. Drill into any line to the underlying groups and ledgers.
  3. Accuracy depends on classification — misgrouped ledgers distort ratios (e.g. loans recorded as current liabilities).

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Category Ratios Profitability Gross margin, net margin, ROE Liquidity Current ratio, quick ratio Efficiency Debtor, inventory, creditor days; cash conversion cycle Solvency Debt-to-equity, interest coverage Tool Alt+G → Ratio Analysis

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Ratios normalise financial statements so businesses of different sizes and periods can be compared. Efficiency ratios link the P&L to the Balance Sheet — revenue and cost flows against the stock, debtors and creditors needed to support them — which is where cash problems usually hide. Because every ratio is computed from grouped balances, sound grouping (Level 1) is the foundation of meaningful analysis.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Using a company from earlier levels (or the sample figures), compute all ratios in the table, open TallyPrime's Ratio Analysis to compare, and write a one-page analysis: three strengths, three concerns and three specific actions (e.g. reduce inventory days by 15).

docs.title: 02 · MIS Reports for Management
docs.text: Owners and managers need concise, regular reports that answer business questions — not a full trial balance. MIS (Management Information System) reporting turns accounting data into decisions. This module designs a monthly MIS pack using TallyPrime reports and exports.

docs.title: 1. What management wants to know
docs.text:
1. How did we do this month vs last month, last year and budget?
  2. Which products, customers, branches and salespeople make (or lose) money?
  3. Do we have enough cash for the next 4–8 weeks?
  4. Who owes us money and how overdue is it? What do we owe?
  5. Is stock healthy — or growing, ageing and tying up cash?

docs.title: 2. The monthly MIS pack
docs.text:
1. Summary dashboard (one page): revenue, gross margin %, net profit, cash and bank balance, receivables, payables, stock value — with change vs last month and budget.
  2. P&L comparison: this month, YTD, budget, variance (TallyPrime P&L with columns and budget).
  3. Sales analysis: by product/stock group, customer, branch (cost centre), salesperson — from Sales Register, Movement Analysis and Cost Centre reports.
  4. Gross profit by item (Stock Item–wise profitability via Movement/Item Analysis or exported data).
  5. Receivables ageing and top 10 overdue customers; payables due in the next 30 days.
  6. Cash flow forecast: opening cash + expected receipts (including post-dated cheques) − planned payments (suppliers, salaries, GST, TDS, EMIs).
  7. Stock: value by group, slow-moving and near-expiry items, reorder needs.
  8. Compliance status: GST, TDS, PF/ESI filings and payments done/pending.

docs.title: 3. Build it efficiently
docs.text:
1. Save configured report views in TallyPrime (F12 options and column settings) for each section.
  2. Export to Excel (Alt+E) into a fixed template where formulas and charts update automatically.
  3. Many businesses use TallyPrime's ODBC/XML data access or third-party connectors to feed Power BI or Google Sheets dashboards (see the Excel and Power BI courses).
  4. Keep definitions consistent (e.g. "gross margin" always after freight inward and discounts).
  5. Deliver within the first 5–7 working days of the month, after reconciliation.

docs.title: 4. Commentary that drives action
docs.text:
1. For each section, write 2–3 bullets: what changed, why, and the recommended action.
  2. Example: "Gross margin fell from 24% to 21% — copper prices rose 9% while selling prices were unchanged. Recommend 5% price revision on wire products from next month."
  3. Highlight exceptions, not everything: variances above ±10%, overdue debts above 90 days, cash shortfall risks.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: MIS section TallyPrime source P&L vs budget P&L with columns + budget Sales analysis Sales Register, Cost Centre, Movement Analysis Receivables/payables Bills Receivable/Payable, ageing Cash forecast Cash/Bank books + Post-Dated Summary Stock Stock Summary, ageing, reorder status Distribution Export to Excel/PDF, email

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: MIS works by aggregating transaction-level data along dimensions management cares about — time, product, customer, location — and comparing it against reference points like budget and prior periods. TallyPrime already stores those dimensions if masters, cost centres and stock groups are set up well, so a good MIS pack is mostly a matter of configuration and consistency. The commentary is what turns reports into management: data explains what happened; analysis explains why and what to do.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Design a monthly MIS pack template for Deccan Furniture Works or Krishna Electricals with the eight sections above. Populate it from your TallyPrime data, build a one-page summary dashboard in Excel, and write the commentary with at least three recommended actions.

docs.title: 03 · Internal Controls, Security & the Edit Log
docs.text: Accounting data is valuable and sensitive. Weak controls lead to errors, fraud and failed audits. This module sets up user security, access rights, period locks and TallyPrime's edit log — which also helps meet the Companies Act requirement for an audit trail.

docs.title: 1. Why controls matter
docs.text:
1. Segregation of duties: the person who records purchases shouldn't approve payments or reconcile the bank.
  2. Authorisation: payments above a limit need approval.
  3. Reconciliation: bank, GST, receivables, payables and stock reconciled regularly.
  4. Audit trail: a record of who changed what and when.
  5. Under the Companies (Accounts) Rules, companies must use accounting software with an audit trail (edit log) that can't be disabled, retained for the statutory period.

docs.title: 2. Users and security in TallyPrime
docs.text:
1. Alt+K → Security Control / Users and Passwords (or Company → Security): enable security and create an administrator (owner) with a strong password.
  2. Define security levels / roles: Data Entry (create vouchers only), Accountant (create, alter, view reports), Auditor (view only), Owner (full).
  3. Restrict access by voucher type, reports, and features (e.g. data entry can't view P&L or alter masters).
  4. Create users with their role; enforce password changes; remove access promptly when people leave.
  5. Enable TallyVault encryption for sensitive data, and keep the vault password secure — it can't be recovered.

docs.title: 3. Edit log and period locks
docs.text:
1. In recent TallyPrime releases, enable Edit Log (for companies it's expected to be on; TallyPrime offers an Edit Log edition/mode where it can't be disabled).
  2. The edit log records creation, alteration and deletion of vouchers and masters with user, date and time, and previous versions.
  3. View it from the voucher (Related Reports → Edit Log) or the Edit Log reports for the company.
  4. Lock periods after closing (e.g. lock entries up to 31 March after audit) so no one alters closed periods; changes require administrator unlock and leave a trace.
  5. Restrict back-dated entries beyond a number of days for data entry users.

docs.title: 4. Practical control checklist
docs.text:
1. Daily: review Day Book for unusual entries; cash count matches books.
  2. Weekly: bank reconciliation; approval of payment batches; review cancelled/deleted vouchers in the edit log.
  3. Monthly: GST and TDS reconciliation; receivables/payables review; stock count samples; MIS review by owner.
  4. Annually: full stock verification, balance confirmations, fixed asset verification, access review.
  5. Keep supporting documents (scans attached or referenced in narrations).

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Control TallyPrime feature Access Users, roles, security levels Encryption TallyVault Audit trail Edit Log Closed periods Lock period / restrict back-dating Review Day Book, edit log reports Segregation Separate roles for entry, approval, reconciliation

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Controls work by making errors and fraud either impossible (access restrictions, locks) or visible (edit logs, reconciliations, reviews). An audit trail changes behaviour: when every alteration is recorded with the user's identity and the original values, quietly manipulating records stops being practical. Auditors rely on these controls to decide how much detailed testing they need — strong controls mean faster, cheaper audits.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Set up security for a company: an owner, an accountant, a data entry operator and an auditor, each with appropriate rights. Enable the edit log, make and alter a voucher as the data entry user, then review the change history as the owner. Write a one-page control checklist for a 10-person business.

docs.title: 04 · Data Management: Backup, Restore & Split
docs.text: Losing accounting data is a disaster — years of records, statutory obligations and audit evidence. This module covers backups, restores, data repair, splitting financial years and moving data between locations in TallyPrime.

docs.title: 1. Where data lives
docs.text:
1. Each company is a numbered folder in TallyPrime's data path (see Alt+Y → Data → Data Path / Company Data settings).
  2. Never edit or copy files while TallyPrime has the company open; use TallyPrime's own backup tools.

docs.title: 2. Backup
docs.text:
1. Alt+Y → Backup (Data menu): choose source companies and a destination (external drive, network folder or a cloud-synced folder).
  2. Schedule backups at least daily for active companies; TallyPrime's auto-backup options and third-party schedulers help.
  3. Follow the 3-2-1 rule: 3 copies, on 2 different media, 1 off-site (e.g. encrypted cloud storage).
  4. Test restores regularly — a backup you can't restore isn't a backup.
  5. Protect backups: encrypt (TallyVault) and restrict access.

docs.title: 3. Restore and repair
docs.text:
1. Alt+Y → Restore: choose the backup file and destination data path; restore to a different path first if you're unsure, to avoid overwriting current data.
  2. If a company shows errors (power cut, disk issue), use Alt+Y → Repair for the company (always back up first).
  3. TallyPrime may also prompt for data migration when moving from older Tally versions (Tally.ERP 9) — follow the migration tool and verify reports before and after.

docs.title: 4. Split company by financial year
docs.text:
1. Over years, data grows large. Alt+Y → Split divides a company into two: up to a date (e.g. 31-3-2026) and from the next day, carrying closing balances (ledgers, bills, stock) forward as opening balances.
  2. Back up before splitting; verify that closing balances in the old company equal opening balances in the new one.
  3. Keep the old company read-only (lock period) for audit and reference.
  4. Alternatively, continue in one company with multiple years — TallyPrime handles this, but split when performance or management requires.

docs.title: 5. Exchanging data
docs.text:
1. Export/Import (Alt+E / Alt+O) masters and vouchers in XML or JSON — useful for branch consolidation, migrations and integrations.
  2. Excel import of masters/vouchers (supported in recent releases) speeds up bulk entry with mapping templates.
  3. Remote access and sync: TallyPrime offers remote access (browser/app via Tally.NET) and sync between branches; cloud hosting options let multiple users access centrally.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Task Path Data path Alt+Y → Data path settings Backup Alt+Y → Backup Restore Alt+Y → Restore (test path first) Repair Alt+Y → Repair (after backup) Split year Alt+Y → Split Export/Import Alt+E / Alt+O

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: TallyPrime stores data in its own database files; its backup tool creates a consistent compressed snapshot while ensuring no half-written transactions are captured, which is why copying folders directly can produce corrupt copies. Splitting creates a new company whose opening balances are generated from the old company's closing position, so the two remain reconcilable. Good data management is invisible when it works — and decisive when hardware fails, ransomware strikes or an auditor asks for records from five years ago.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Back up a practice company to an external location, restore it to a different data path and verify its Balance Sheet matches. Split it at a year-end date and confirm closing and opening balances agree. Write a backup policy for a small business (frequency, locations, encryption, test schedule, responsibility).

docs.title: 05 · The Annual Compliance Calendar
docs.text: Indian businesses face recurring deadlines across GST, income tax, TDS/TCS, payroll and company law. Missing them costs interest, late fees and penalties — and damages credibility. This module builds an annual compliance calendar. Dates are typical as of 2026; confirm current due dates and any extensions on official portals.

docs.title: 1. Monthly
docs.text: Due Compliance 7th Deposit TDS/TCS deducted in the previous month (March: 30 April) 11th GSTR-1 (monthly filers) 13th IFF / GSTR-1 (QRMP quarterly) 15th PF and ESI contributions and returns (ECR) 20th GSTR-3B (monthly filers) 22nd/24th GSTR-3B (QRMP, quarterly, state-wise) 25th PMT-06 GST payment (QRMP, months 1 and 2) State dates Professional tax payment/returns

docs.title: 2. Quarterly
docs.text:
1. TDS/TCS statements: 31 July, 31 October, 31 January, 31 May; TCS statements a little earlier (15th after the quarter, historically).
  2. TDS certificates to payees after statements are processed.
  3. Advance tax instalments (if tax liability above threshold): 15 June (15%), 15 September (45%), 15 December (75%), 15 March (100%).
  4. Composition dealers: CMP-08 by the 18th after each quarter.
  5. Review: GST reconciliation, receivables ageing, stock verification samples.

docs.title: 3. Annual
docs.text:
1. GSTR-9/9C: 31 December.
  2. Income tax returns: non-audit cases typically 31 July; tax audit cases 31 October (tax audit report by 30 September); transfer pricing cases 30 November — check each year.
  3. Company law (ROC): AGM within 6 months of year-end (by 30 September); AOC-4 (financial statements) within 30 days of AGM; MGT-7/7A (annual return) within 60 days of AGM; DIR-3 KYC for directors; MSME-1 half-yearly if payments to MSMEs are overdue.
  4. LLP: Form 11 (by 30 May) and Form 8 (by 30 October).
  5. Statutory audit, stock verification, balance confirmations, fixed asset verification.
  6. Renewals: trade licences, shop and establishment registration, professional tax enrolment, insurance.
  7. GST: LUT for exports for the new year (before the first export), ITC-04 for job work as applicable.

docs.title: 4. Build and run the calendar
docs.text:
1. Create a calendar (Google Calendar/Outlook or a task tool) with recurring reminders 5 and 2 days before each deadline.
  2. Assign an owner and a backup for each item.
  3. Maintain a compliance tracker: period, due date, filed date, acknowledgement number, challan details, remarks.
  4. Use TallyPrime reports (GST, TDS, payroll) to prepare data; keep acknowledgements and challans with the records.
  5. Review monthly with the owner: filed, pending, any notices received.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Area Key deadlines GST 11th (GSTR-1), 20th (GSTR-3B), 31 Dec (GSTR-9) TDS/TCS 7th deposit; quarterly statements Payroll 15th PF/ESI Income tax Advance tax quarterly; ITR by due date Company law AGM, AOC-4, MGT-7 Tool Calendar + compliance tracker

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Each compliance date is the end of a chain of upstream work — accurate entries, reconciliations, approvals and payments — so the calendar is really a production schedule for the finance function. Businesses that miss deadlines usually fail upstream (late entries, unreconciled data), not on filing day. A tracker with acknowledgements also becomes the evidence pack when notices arrive, often years later.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Build a 12-month compliance calendar and tracker for Krishna Electricals (a private limited company with GST monthly returns, TDS, payroll and exports). Include owners, reminders and the TallyPrime report used for each item. Mark the five deadlines with the highest penalty risk and explain why.

docs.title: 06 · Accounting for Startups & MSMEs
docs.text: Small businesses and startups have specific accounting needs: choosing a business structure, keeping founders' and business money separate, managing cash runway, using government MSME benefits and preparing for investors or lenders. This module covers the essentials. (General guidance — consult a CA for your situation.)

docs.title: 1. Business structure
docs.text:
1. Sole proprietorship — simplest; owner taxed personally; unlimited liability.
  2. Partnership / LLP — shared ownership; LLP offers limited liability with lighter compliance than a company.
  3. Private limited company — separate legal entity, limited liability, easier to raise equity; more compliance (ROC filings, audit).
  4. The structure affects tax rates, compliance, fundraising and how TallyPrime capital accounts are set up (capital account vs share capital and reserves).

docs.title: 2. Clean books from day one
docs.text:
1. Separate bank account for the business; avoid personal expenses through the business (record them as drawings if they happen).
  2. Founders' loans to the company: record as unsecured loans with documentation, not capital, unless shares are issued.
  3. Record every invoice and expense with documents; claim GST ITC properly.
  4. Choose accounting policies early: revenue recognition, depreciation, stock valuation.

docs.title: 3. MSME registration and benefits
docs.text:
1. Udyam Registration (udyamregistration.gov.in) — free, PAN/Aadhaar-based. Classification (revised 2025) by investment and turnover: micro, small and medium enterprises with higher limits than before — check current thresholds.
  2. Benefits: priority sector lending, collateral-free loans under the CGTMSE scheme, government tender preferences, and protection against delayed payments.
  3. Delayed payment protection: buyers must pay MSME suppliers within the agreed period (maximum 45 days); under income-tax rules, payments to micro and small enterprises beyond the limit are disallowed as expenses until paid (section 43B(h) under the earlier Act, carried into the new law) — a reason buyers prioritise MSME invoices.
  4. Record supplier MSME status in TallyPrime ledgers (MSME registration details) to track payment timelines and report outstanding dues (MSME-1 for companies).

docs.title: 4. Startup finance essentials
docs.text:
1. Burn rate = monthly cash outflow − inflow; runway = cash balance ÷ net burn. ₹60 lakh cash with ₹5 lakh monthly net burn = 12 months.
  2. Monthly MIS with unit economics (CAC, gross margin, contribution per order) for founders and investors.
  3. DPIIT recognition under Startup India offers benefits like tax holiday eligibility (section 80-IAC criteria under the earlier Act, with corresponding provisions), self-certification under labour laws and faster patent processing.
  4. Equity rounds: record share capital and securities premium; maintain a cap table; ESOPs need careful accounting and tax treatment.
  5. Investor due diligence expects clean, reconciled books, filed returns and statutory compliance — often the most expensive problem to fix late.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Topic Key point Structure Proprietorship / LLP / Pvt Ltd trade-offs Separation Business bank account; drawings for personal use Founder loans Unsecured loans, documented Udyam Free MSME registration; benefits MSME payments Within 45 days; tax disallowance if late Runway Cash ÷ net monthly burn

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Small businesses fail more often from running out of cash than from lack of profit. Clean, separate books make cash visible, support credit and funding applications, and keep tax deductions defensible. MSME payment rules shift bargaining power toward small suppliers by attaching tax consequences to late payment, which is why accurate MSME tagging of suppliers in TallyPrime now matters to buyers as well.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: For a new startup (your choice), recommend a business structure with reasons, set up a TallyPrime company with appropriate capital/loan ledgers, record founder funding as equity and loan, tag two suppliers as MSME, and calculate runway from a 6-month cash forecast. List the registrations needed in the first 90 days.

docs.title: 07 · Moving to an ERP: Tally, Zoho, SAP & Oracle
docs.text: As businesses grow, they sometimes outgrow standalone accounting software and move to an ERP (enterprise resource planning) system that integrates finance with sales, procurement, manufacturing, HR and more. This module helps you judge when to move, compare options and run a migration.

docs.title: 1. Signs you may need more than TallyPrime alone
docs.text:
1. Many users across locations needing real-time access and complex approval workflows.
  2. Complex manufacturing (MRP, shop-floor control), large warehouses, or multi-company consolidation with intercompany eliminations.
  3. Heavy integrations: e-commerce, CRM, payment gateways, logistics, banks.
  4. Investor or group reporting needs (Ind AS, global parent reporting).
  5. Note: TallyPrime itself scales well for many SMEs with add-ons, TallyPrime Server, connectors and APIs — moving is a business decision, not a default.

docs.title: 2. Common options
docs.text: System Typical fit TallyPrime (+ extensions) SMEs; strong Indian compliance; low cost; widely known by accountants Zoho Books / Zoho One Cloud-first SMEs and startups; good integrations; GST and e-invoicing support Busy, Marg Indian SMEs (trading, pharma distribution) Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central / Odoo Growing mid-size businesses wanting a broader ERP Oracle NetSuite Fast-growing companies, multi-entity, global operations SAP Business One Mid-size businesses SAP S/4HANA, Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP Large enterprises, complex operations, group reporting

docs.title: 3. Evaluate properly
docs.text:
1. List requirements by priority: must-have (GST, e-invoicing, TDS, payroll integration, inventory), should-have, nice-to-have.
  2. Total cost of ownership over 5 years: licences/subscriptions, implementation partner, customisation, training, hardware/cloud, support.
  3. Ask for demos using your scenarios (a GST invoice with e-way bill, a job work cycle, month-end close).
  4. Check partner experience in your industry and references.
  5. Consider people: accountant availability and training for the chosen system.

docs.title: 4. Run the migration
docs.text:
1. Choose a cut-over date — usually the start of a financial year or quarter.
  2. Clean data in TallyPrime first: remove duplicate ledgers, fix groupings, close old bills.
  3. Migrate masters (chart of accounts, parties with GSTINs, items with HSN), opening balances (ledger, bill-wise, stock by godown/batch) and optionally historical transactions.
  4. Run parallel for one period in both systems; reconcile trial balances, receivables, payables, stock and GST outputs.
  5. Train users, document new processes, and keep TallyPrime data read-only for history and audits.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Step Key action Decide Business need, not trend Requirements Must/should/nice-to-have Cost 5-year TCO Demo Your real scenarios Migrate Clean data, masters, opening balances Validate Parallel run + reconciliations

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: An ERP replaces separate systems and spreadsheets with one database shared by every department, so a sales order can automatically reserve stock, trigger procurement and post accounting entries. That integration delivers control and real-time visibility but brings complexity and cost; many ERP problems come from migrating messy data or redesigning processes poorly. Accountants who understand both TallyPrime and ERP concepts are valuable bridges during these transitions.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: For a growing manufacturer with three plants and an online store, write an ERP evaluation: 15 prioritised requirements, a shortlist of three systems with pros/cons, an estimated 5-year cost comparison (use publicly available pricing where possible), and a migration plan with cut-over date and validation checks.

docs.title: 08 · Running an Accounting Practice
docs.text: Many trained accountants serve multiple small businesses — as freelancers, bookkeeping firms or alongside a CA practice. This module covers services, pricing, client management, tools and professional boundaries.

docs.title: 1. Services you can offer
docs.text:
1. Bookkeeping in TallyPrime: monthly entries, bank reconciliation, receivables/payables.
  2. GST compliance: GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, reconciliations, e-invoicing setup, annual return preparation support.
  3. TDS compliance: computations, deposits, quarterly statement preparation.
  4. Payroll processing: salaries, PF/ESI, payslips.
  5. MIS reporting and cash flow forecasts for owners.
  6. TallyPrime setup, migration and training for businesses.
  7. Note: certain services — statutory audits, tax audits, certification, some representations — are reserved for Chartered Accountants or other authorised professionals. Partner with a CA for those.

docs.title: 2. Pricing and engagement
docs.text:
1. Price by package and volume: e.g. monthly bookkeeping + GST for up to 150 transactions; add-ons for TDS, payroll, MIS.
  2. Write an engagement letter: scope, client responsibilities (documents by the 5th), timelines, fees, payment terms, data confidentiality, limitations of responsibility.
  3. Collect fees monthly in advance or by mandate; stop work policy for overdue fees.
  4. Register for GST when your turnover crosses the threshold (₹20 lakh for services in most states) and issue proper invoices.

docs.title: 3. Workflow and tools
docs.text:
1. Document collection: shared folders (Google Drive/OneDrive), WhatsApp Business catalogues for checklists, or client portals; a monthly document checklist per client.
  2. Remote access: TallyPrime remote access or cloud hosting to work on client data securely; never keep client data on personal devices without encryption.
  3. Task tracker for every client and deadline (from Module 5's compliance calendar).
  4. Standard procedures: month-end checklist, review by a second person, query lists sent to clients.
  5. Data security and confidentiality: access only what's needed, strong passwords, backups, clear data-return terms when engagements end (DPDP obligations apply to personal data you handle).

docs.title: 4. Grow and retain clients
docs.text:
1. Niche by industry (restaurants, traders, clinics, startups) to work faster and market better.
  2. Get clients through referrals from CAs, local business networks, LinkedIn, and helpful content (GST updates in plain language).
  3. Deliver value beyond compliance: monthly MIS with insights, cash flow alerts, tax-saving reminders.
  4. Communicate proactively about deadlines and changes; respond within an agreed time.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Area Practice Services Bookkeeping, GST, TDS, payroll, MIS, Tally setup Boundaries Audit/certification via CAs Engagement letter Scope, responsibilities, fees, confidentiality Workflow Checklists, trackers, review Security Remote access, encryption, minimal access Growth Niche, referrals, value-added MIS

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: An accounting practice is a production system: inputs (client documents) arrive on a schedule, processes (entry, reconciliation, review) convert them into outputs (books, returns, reports) by statutory deadlines. Standardisation — checklists, templates, niches — is what makes it profitable and reliable, because each client stops being a custom project. Clear engagement terms protect both sides when documents arrive late or responsibilities blur.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Design a service menu with three packages and prices for small businesses in your city, write an engagement letter template, a monthly document checklist for a trading client, and a month-end checklist for your team. Define your target niche and three ways you'll acquire your first five clients.

docs.title: 09 · Career Paths: Accountant to Finance Manager
docs.text: TallyPrime and GST skills open many doors in India's accounting and finance job market. This module maps career paths, skills, qualifications and how to present your experience to employers.

docs.title: 1. Typical roles and progression
docs.text:
1. Accounts Assistant / Junior Accountant — data entry, vouchers, bank reconciliation, filing.
  2. Accountant — full books, GST and TDS compliance, payroll, month-end close.
  3. Senior Accountant / Accounts Executive (GST/Taxation) — reconciliations, returns, audit coordination, MIS.
  4. Accounts Manager / Finance Manager — team leadership, budgeting, cash flow, statutory compliance, banking relationships.
  5. Financial Controller / CFO (often with professional qualifications) — strategy, funding, governance.
  6. Parallel paths: shared services and GCC roles (R2R, P2P, O2C processes on ERPs like SAP and Oracle), tax consulting, audit firms, freelancing/practice (Module 8).

docs.title: 2. Skills employers look for
docs.text:
1. TallyPrime proficiency including GST, TDS, payroll, inventory and reports.
  2. GST end to end: invoicing, ITC reconciliation, GSTR-1/3B/9, e-invoicing, e-way bills.
  3. Advanced Excel: lookups, pivot tables, reconciliation techniques (see the Excel Mastery Path).
  4. Month-end close discipline and accuracy; documentation.
  5. Communication with auditors, vendors and management; MIS commentary.
  6. ERP exposure (SAP FICO, Oracle, Zoho) for larger companies.

docs.title: 3. Qualifications and certifications
docs.text:
1. B.Com / M.Com / BBA — the usual base.
  2. Professional: CA, CMA, CS (India); ACCA, CPA (international roles).
  3. Short certifications: Tally's official certification programmes, GST practitioner courses, SAP FICO training.
  4. Experience with real books (internships, family business, practice firm) often matters as much as certificates.

docs.title: 4. Present your experience
docs.text:
1. Build a portfolio from this course: the projects (monthly books, GST month, quarter-end close, full-year capstone) with reports exported.
  2. Write a results-focused resume: "Reconciled GSTR-2B monthly for 3 entities, recovering ₹4.2 lakh of missed ITC" or "Reduced month-end close from 10 days to 5."
  3. Use the job's keywords honestly — GST, TDS, R2R, reconciliation, MIS, the ERP named — and tailor your resume to each role. The Mastery Path Resume Tools give you a free ATS keyword check against any job description.
  4. Prepare for practical tests: record vouchers, compute GST and TDS, reconcile a bank statement in TallyPrime within a time limit.
  5. Interview questions to expect: golden rules, ITC conditions, GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B, TDS sections and rates, depreciation methods, how you'd handle a supplier missing in GSTR-2B.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Role Core responsibilities Junior accountant Vouchers, reconciliation Accountant Books, GST, TDS, payroll Senior accountant Returns, audits, MIS Finance manager Budgets, cash, team, compliance R2R/GCC roles Close, reconciliations on ERPs Proof Projects, quantified resume, practical tests

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: Employers hire accountants to reduce risk and increase visibility: accurate books, on-time compliance and clear reports. Your career advances as you move from recording transactions to owning processes, then to interpreting results and advising decisions. Demonstrating that progression — with quantified examples and practical skill — is what distinguishes candidates in a market where many list "Tally" on their resume.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Pick a target role and collect three job descriptions. Build a skills-gap list, assemble a portfolio with your four course projects, and rewrite your resume with five quantified achievements. Practise a 30-minute TallyPrime test: record 15 vouchers with GST and TDS, then reconcile the bank.

docs.title: 10 · Capstone — A Full Year of Books & Compliance
docs.text: Your capstone demonstrates complete mastery: a full financial year of books and compliance for a GST-registered business in TallyPrime, ending with year-end close, analysis and management reporting. Use Annapurna Spices Pvt Ltd, Indore (Madhya Pradesh), a manufacturer and trader of packaged spices with domestic and export sales — or a real business you're authorised to work on.

docs.title: 1. Setup (start of year)
docs.text:
1. Company with GST (monthly), e-invoicing (assume turnover above ₹5 crore), e-way bills, TDS, TCS, payroll, inventory with godowns and batches (with expiry dates), BOMs, multi-currency, cost centres (Plant, Sales, Admin), budgets.
  2. Opening balances from the previous year's Balance Sheet (provided or created), including bill-wise receivables/payables and batch-wise stock.
  3. Security roles and edit log enabled; backup policy in place; compliance calendar created.

docs.title: 2. Through the year (record at least one representative month per quarter in full, and summarise others)
docs.text:
1. Purchases (domestic, inter-state, import), production with BOMs, job work for packaging.
  2. Sales (B2B intra/inter-state, B2C, exports under LUT, marketplace sales with GST TCS and TDS).
  3. Credit/debit notes, RCM transactions, e-invoices and e-way bills.
  4. Payroll with PF/ESI/PT; TDS on contractors, professionals and rent; TCS where applicable.
  5. Banking: e-payments, PDCs, reconciliation every month.
  6. Monthly GSTR-1/3B with GSTR-2B reconciliation; quarterly TDS statements; PF/ESI filings.
  7. Monthly MIS packs against budget.

docs.title: 3. Year-end
docs.text:
1. Adjustments: depreciation (book and tax note), outstanding/prepaid, accrued income, provisions, stock verification and write-downs.
  2. Forex restatement of open foreign balances.
  3. GSTR-9 (and 9C data) reconciliation; ITC reversals for unpaid suppliers.
  4. Final Trial Balance, P&L, Balance Sheet, cash flow, ratio analysis.
  5. Lock the year, back up, and split the company into the new financial year.

docs.title: 4. Deliverables
docs.text: Deliverable Done? Company setup + opening balances + controls Representative months fully recorded (4) Monthly bank and GST reconciliations TDS/TCS and payroll compliance records Year-end adjustments + forex restatement GSTR-9 reconciliation Final statements + ratio analysis Annual MIS report with recommendations Backup + split into new year

docs.title: How It Actually Works
docs.text: A full accounting year is the complete cycle every finance team runs: set up, record, reconcile, comply, adjust, close, report and roll forward. Each module of this course is one part of that cycle; the capstone shows you can run them together under real deadlines and dependencies. It's also your strongest proof for employers and clients — a documented year of books and compliance demonstrates far more than any certificate.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: Complete the capstone and prepare a 10-slide presentation for the company's directors covering: the year's performance vs budget, key ratios with interpretation, compliance status (all filings and payments), three control or process improvements you implemented, and recommendations for next year. Add it to your portfolio alongside the exported reports.
